```bash
cd /home/mantmant/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/.specstory && python3 - <<'EOF'
block = '''
### Decisions for Commit 2
#### Decision 2: The commit picker declares `c` itself, and `c` only ever opens it

**Decision:** The commit picker on the "Files changed" tab adds its own `c` shortcut when it appears on the page. Pressing `c` opens the picker the same way a click does, and does nothing when it is already open.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A new general attribute in the page's HTML that makes a shortcut click an element, like the one #58 added for links. (b) The page code that sets up the picker adds `c` from outside and clicks the picker's button.
**Rationale:** The picker's button is built by the picker itself after the page loads, and a click opens or closes it. Only the picker knows whether it is open, and it already has its translated label ("Filter by commit"). Declaring `c` inside the picker lets `c` open it through the same steps a click takes, so the first entry gets focus and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click (AC4), without ever closing it by accident. (a) would add a general mechanism for a single use, would have to reach inside the picker for a button that doesn't exist until the picker is built, and a click would close an open picker. (b) has the same closing problem and depends on the picker's inner markup from outside it.
**Consequences:** `c` only exists while the picker is on the page, so it is missing on the compare page and on an issue's own page (AC5). The picker gets its section ("Pull Requests", an existing string) from the page, the same way the "Go to file" box got its section in #56. This is the first shortcut a component adds from its own code instead of from the page's HTML.
'''
for p in ['issue-59-design-decisions.md', 'decisions.md']:
    s = open(p).read().rstrip('\n') + '\n' + block
    open(p, 'w').write(s)
EOF

Commit 2 is ready in the sandbox for you to review: `c` on "Files changed" opens the commit picker.

**Decision 2** is appended to both your `decisions.md` and my `issue-59-design-decisions.md`.

**What changed**
- **`templates/repo/diff/box.tmpl`:** `#diff-commit-select` gets `data-shortcut-section` from the existing `pull_requests` key ("Pull Requests"). That's the same way #56 handed the "Go to file" box its section.
- **`web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.vue`:** the component reads that attribute next to its other ones. In `mounted()`, it registers `c`, tied to its own element and described with its existing "Filter by commit" label. The action is `if (!this.menuVisible) this.toggleMenu()`, with a same-line comment saying why: it opens like a click but never closes an open menu.

**Checked**
- `make lint-js` passes, including `vue-tsc`.
- **Real pull request on the sandbox: 13/13.** It used a throwaway repo, deleted afterwards. It checked:
  - `c` opens the picker with focus on its first entry (AC4), and pressing `c` again leaves it open.
  - Escape closes it and puts focus back on the button.
  - `c` and a mouse click give identical focus steps through the arrow keys (AC4).
  - The label is "Filter by commit" in "Pull Requests" (AC6).
  - `g c` on the tab still goes to the front page (AC5).
  - `c` does nothing on an issue page, the compare page or the PR's conversation tab (AC5), and there are no JS errors.

**Two things worth knowing**
- **Label:** the first entry is labelled "Show all commits". AC4 and your reviewer call it "Show all changes", after the code's `showAllChanges`. The checks target the entry itself, so this only matters for the PR wording.
- **Possible tech debt:** after a click or `c`, ArrowDown stops on the "hold Shift for a range" hint text before reaching the commits. That's the picker's existing behaviour, and the spec puts changing the picker out of scope. I noted it as a candidate "Encountered" item in `.specstory/issue-59-tech-debt.md`. Keep it or drop it.

export async function apiCreateFile(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, repo: string, filepath: string, content: string, {branch, newBranch, message}: {branch?: string; newBranch?: string; message?: string} = {}) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/contents/${filepath}`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
    data: {content: Buffer.from(content, 'utf8').toString('base64'), branch, new_branch: newBranch, message},
  }), 'apiCreateFile');
}

export async function apiCreateBranch(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, repo: string, newBranch: string) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/branches`, {
    headers: apiHeaders(),
    data: {new_branch_name: newBranch},
  }), 'apiCreateBranch');
}

/** Create a PR via API. Returns the PR index for subsequent operations. */
export async function apiCreatePR(requestContext: APIRequestContext, owner: string, repo: string, head: string, base: string, title: string, {headers}: {headers?: Record<string, string>} = {}): Promise<number> {
  let prIndex = 0;
  await apiRetry(async () => {
    const response = await requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls`, {
      headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
      data: {head, base, title},
    });
    if (response.ok()) prIndex = (await response.json()).number;
    return response;
  }, 'apiCreatePR');
  return prIndex;
}

# web_src/js/components — the Vue 3 components

**Read when:** building or changing an interactive widget complex enough to need state.
**Not here:** how a component gets mounted -> `frontend-js.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`.

## Responsibilities

Vue 3 single-file components for the parts of the UI too stateful for a Go template plus a little
JavaScript: the Actions run viewer, the diff file tree, the dashboard repo list, the merge form,
the various repo charts.

`docs/guidelines-frontend.md` draws the line as: **Go templates for simple and SEO-relevant pages,
Vue for complex interactive pages.** A page that only needs a toggle does not need Vue.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/components/RepoActionView.vue` | the Actions run log viewer |
| `web_src/js/components/DiffFileTree.vue`, `DiffFileTreeItem.vue` | the code-review file tree |
| `web_src/js/components/PullRequestMergeForm.vue` | the merge button and its options |
| `web_src/js/components/DashboardRepoList.vue` | the dashboard repo list |
| `web_src/js/components/ViewFileTreeStore.ts` | a plain-TS store shared by the file-tree components |
| `web_src/js/components/ActionRunView.ts`, `WorkflowGraph.utils.ts` | logic extracted out of the neighbouring `.vue` files so it is unit-testable |
| `web_src/js/components/*.test.ts` | Vitest tests, colocated |

## Conventions & invariants

- Filenames are PascalCase and match the component name.
- **Components do not mount themselves.** A `features/` module does it, guarded by the presence of
  its root element:

  ```ts
  const el = document.querySelector('#repo-contributors-chart');
  if (!el) return;
  createApp(RepoContributors, {repoLink: el.getAttribute('data-repo-link')}).mount(el);
  ```

  So adding a component always means touching `frontend-js.md`'s wiring too.
- Props come from `data-*` attributes read with `getAttribute`, or from `window.config.pageData`
  (set by the handler via `ctx.PageData`, see `templates.md`). Do not fetch configuration the
  server could have handed you.
- Show and hide with `v-if` / `v-show` — not `.tw-hidden`, which is the plain-JS mechanism.
- **Do not mix Vue with Fomantic-UI JavaScript.** Fomantic's CSS classes are fine; its jQuery
  behaviours fight Vue's ownership of the DOM.
- No JSX — SFCs only.
- Data fetching still goes through `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`.
- Logic worth testing is pulled into a sibling `.ts` file and tested there; the `.vue` file stays
  presentational. `ActionRunView.ts` beside `RepoActionView.vue` is the pattern.

## Recipes

**Add a component.** Create `YourThing.vue`, a mount block in the owning `features/` module,
a root element with the data attributes it needs in the template, and — if it has real logic — a
sibling `.ts` with a `.test.ts`.

**Give a component server data.** Small values as `data-*` attributes on the mount point; anything
structured via `ctx.PageData` in the handler, read as `window.config.pageData`.

**Test one.** `pnpm exec vitest <name>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A component with no mount call is dead code that still ships in the bundle — the compiler will
  not tell you.
- `.ts` files in this directory are not components; they are stores and extracted logic. Do not
  assume everything here is a `.vue`.
- Because mounting is element-guarded, a typo in the root element's id or class fails silently:
  nothing renders and nothing errors.

## Related

- `frontend-js.md` — the `features/` module that mounts the component
- `templates.md` — the mount point and `pageData`
```

```text
3045482068 docs(context): update claude-student docs for frontend vue (#59)
Title: feat(shortcut): g shortcuts for the repository tabs and notifications

Closes #58

## What changed and why

GitHub users move around a repository with two-key `g` shortcuts, and Gitea had none. Building on #56's registry, this PR adds them: `g c`, `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` go to a repository's Code, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions and Wiki tabs, and `g n` goes to the user's notifications from any page.

- **A link can declare its own shortcut.** A link in a template that carries a few attributes registers a shortcut that goes where the link leads. The shortcut only exists while the link is on the page, so it follows whatever the template already decides about the link.
- **The tab bar declares the repository shortcuts.** Each tab marks itself, so a tab that isn't shown (its feature is turned off, the user can't read it, or it is Actions on an empty repository) has no shortcut. The external issue tracker and external wiki tabs aren't marked, so a shortcut never leaves Gitea. Tabs that move into the "more" menu on a narrow window are still on the page, so their shortcuts keep working.
- **`g c` goes to the repository's front page,** not where the Code tab links: on a branch other than the default, the Code tab points at that branch.
- **`g n` is declared on the notifications bell,** which only signed-in users have. The bell is in the page twice, once for phones and once for desktops, so only one copy declares it.
- **Each shortcut is listed with its tab's translated name** ("Issues", without the open count), in the "Repository" section with `s` and `t`. `g n` is "Notifications" under a new "General" string, which #57's help dialog will also use for `?`.
- The docs in `.claude-students` are updated with the new way to add a shortcut.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` on a repository page go to that tab.
- **AC2:** `g c` goes to the repository's front page on the default branch, even while browsing another branch.
- **AC3:** a tab that is not shown declares no shortcut, so its keys do nothing.
- **AC4:** the external tracker and wiki tabs declare no shortcut, so `g i` and `g w` do nothing there and the browser stays in Gitea.
- **AC5:** tabs in the "more" menu are still on the page, so their shortcuts work.
- **AC6:** signed in, `g n` goes to notifications from any page; signed out there is no bell, so it does nothing.
- **AC7:** outside a repository there is no tab bar, so the repository shortcuts do nothing.
- **AC8:** each repository shortcut has its tab's name in the Repository section, and `g n` is "Notifications" under "General".

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

Most of the risk in this PR is in the wiring, not the code: whether a shortcut exists is decided by the templates, so most mistakes only show up on a real page. The tests are split along that line.

- **Unit tests (Vitest) for the part that is plain code.** Turning a link into a shortcut needs no server, so it is tested on its own, where the tests are fast and a failure points straight at the cause. The 4 new tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` target the three places where the obvious version would be wrong: a description taken from the link's text would include the open count, following the link would keep `g c` on the browsed branch, and treating a hidden link as gone would break the "more" menu. They are named `#58 AC…`, because the other tests in that file use #56's AC numbers.
- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** A unit test can't see which tabs a template renders. Each of the 4 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the one situation where a wiring mistake would show: a branch other than the default, the only time `g c` and the Code tab disagree; turned-off and external tabs, the only time a shortcut could outlive its tab or leave Gitea; a narrow window, the only time tabs move; and a signed-in user, the only time there are two bells to clash. On an ordinary page each of these mistakes would pass unnoticed. A new `apiEditRepo` helper in `tests/e2e/utils.ts` sets up the repository with the turned-off and external tabs.
- **Proving that nothing happened.** A test that presses a dead shortcut and sees nothing would also pass on a page where no key works at all. The AC3 and AC4 test therefore presses a live shortcut (`s`) after the dead ones and checks that it still runs.

**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real. For the unit tests: taking the description from the link's text, dropping the section, an action that does nothing, ignoring a link's own address, and treating a hidden part of the page as gone. For the Playwright tests: the Code tab without its own address, a shortcut on the external tracker tab, both bells declaring `g n`, and treating hidden elements as gone. Each break failed the matching tests, and #56's tests stayed green.

**Not covered automatically, and why.** AC3's other cases, a tab the user can't read and Actions on an empty repository, aren't driven separately. The template hides those tabs the same way it hides a turned-off one, which the AC3 test covers.

**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: the tab shortcuts, `g c` from a branch, a narrow window, and `g n` signed in and out. I spot checked the shortcuts myself as well.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` each go to their tab on a real repository; a link's shortcut goes where the link leads |
| AC2 | On a branch other than the default, the Code tab links to that branch and `g c` goes to the front page; a link's shortcut can go to its own address |
| AC3 | With pull requests and Actions turned off, no `g p` or `g a` is declared, the keys do nothing and a live shortcut still runs after them |
| AC4 | With an external tracker and wiki, their tabs are shown but declare nothing, the keys do nothing and no new tab opens |
| AC5 | At 420 px wide the Wiki tab is in the "more" menu and `g w` still works; a link moved into a hidden part of the page keeps its shortcut |
| AC6 | Signed out there is no `g n`; signed in there is exactly one, and it goes to notifications |
| AC7 | On `/explore/repos` no repository shortcut is declared |
| AC8 | Issues is "Issues" in "Repository", and `g n` is "Notifications" in "General"; a link is listed with its own description, not its text |

## CI / manual verification

- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.
- `make test-frontend`: 361 tests pass, including the 4 new ones.
- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates`, `make lint-editorconfig` and the locale JSON lint pass.
- The 7 Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` pass locally on Chromium and Firefox; each new one runs in under 1.5 s.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` reports only the two `models-issues.md` size limits, which were failing before this PR.

## Design

Design decisions noted under issue #58.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- `g n` and the tabs in the "more" menu rely on #56 counting a hidden element as present. The bell that declares `g n` is the phone-layout copy, which is hidden on desktops, and tabs in the closed "more" menu are hidden too. If the registry ever started ignoring hidden elements, as #56's Tech Debt suggests later shortcuts might need, both would stop working. The Playwright tests for AC5 and AC6 fail if that happens.

**Encountered:**
- The navbar renders its icons, the notifications bell among them, twice: once for the phone layout and once for desktop, with CSS hiding one. For a signed-in user both copies are in the page, unless they must change their password first, so marking both with `g n` makes #56's registry throw a clash on every page. Handled by a `WithShortcut` flag that only the copy rendered for every signed-in user passes. The core issue of two notification bells was not fixed here.

## Implementation Note
Despite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. As confusing as this may be, these shortcuts only take the user to another page, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes, and ran the headless-browser checks and the checks that each test fails when its code is broken. Title: feat(shortcut): c shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the commit picker

Closes #59

## What changed and why

On GitHub, `c` starts a new issue or pull request from the list, and opens the commit picker on a pull request's changed files. Gitea had no such shortcut. Building on #56's registry and #58's link shortcuts, this PR adds `c` in those three places.

- **The create buttons declare `c` themselves.** "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are links, so they declare `c` the same way #58's tabs declare their `g` shortcuts, and `c` goes where the button leads, exactly as a click would. When the repository uses issue templates, that is the template chooser.
- **Only a button that really creates something declares it.** An archived repository has no create button, and its pull request list shows "Compare commits" in that place; a "New Pull Request" button the user can't use is greyed out. The list page already decides all of this, so in each of these cases `c` simply doesn't exist.
- **The commit picker declares `c` itself.** It is a Vue component that builds its own button, so it adds `c` when it appears on the "Files changed" tab. `c` opens it the same way a click does, with focus on its first entry, and never closes it.
- **Each `c` is listed with what it opens** ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab, using existing strings, so nothing new needs translating.
- The docs in `.claude-students` describe how a component adds its own shortcut.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** `c` on the issue list goes where "New Issue" leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser.
- **AC2:** `c` on the pull request list goes where "New Pull Request" leads.
- **AC3:** a greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, and an archived repository's lists, declare no `c`, so it does nothing.
- **AC4:** on the "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the commit picker with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click.
- **AC5:** `c` only exists on those three pages, so it does nothing elsewhere; when `c` is the second key of `g c`, only `g c` runs.
- **AC6:** each `c` is described by what it opens, under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

Almost all of this PR is wiring: which button declares `c` is decided by the list page, and the commit picker only exists on a real pull request. So the tests are Playwright tests on real pages.

- **No new unit tests, and why.** The only new code is a two-line action in the commit picker. #58's unit tests already cover a link turning into a shortcut, and the registry's handling of `c` inside `g c` is covered by #56's. A unit test of the picker would have to fake its loading of the commits and its focus handling, so it would mostly test the fakes.
- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** Each of the 3 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the situation where a mistake would show. A signed-in user, because only then is "New Pull Request" usable. A signed-out visitor and an archived repository, the only times the button is greyed out or replaced by "Compare commits", which looks the same as the create button to the page code. A real pull request's "Files changed" tab, the only place the picker exists and the only way to see where focus lands.
- **What "nothing happens" means here.** For AC3 the tests check that the page declares no `c`, instead of pressing `c` and waiting to see that nothing happened. Showing that a key didn't start a navigation races with whatever is pressed next, and whether `c` exists is decided by the declaration alone.

**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real: declaring `c` on the greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, declaring it on "Compare commits" in an archived repository, removing it from "New Issue", and letting `c` close an open picker. Each break failed the matching test, and #56's and #58's tests stayed green.

**Not covered automatically, and why.** The template chooser isn't driven separately: "New Issue" links to it itself, and `c` goes wherever that link points. `c` doing nothing on an issue's own page, the compare page and a pull request's conversation tab was checked by hand, since there is no picker or create button there to declare it.

**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: both lists signed in and out, an archived repository, and a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, where `c` and a mouse click gave the same focus steps through the arrow keys.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | On the issue list, `c` goes to the new issue page |
| AC2 | On the pull request list, `c` goes where "New Pull Request" leads |
| AC3 | Signed out, the greyed-out "New Pull Request" declares no `c`; in an archived repository neither list declares `c`, though "Compare commits" is shown |
| AC4 | On a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the picker with focus on its first entry, `c` again leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to its button |
| AC5 | On the issue list, `g c` goes to the front page instead of starting a new issue |
| AC6 | "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are in "Issues"; the picker's section is "Pull Requests" |

## CI / manual verification

- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.
- `make test-frontend`: 361 tests pass.
- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.
- The 10 Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` pass locally on Chromium and Firefox; each new one runs in under 1.5 s.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` reports only the two `models-issues.md` size limits, which were failing before this PR.

## Design

Design decisions noted under issue #59.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- None.

**Encountered:**
- In the commit picker on "Files changed", ArrowDown from the first entry stops on the "hold Shift for a range" hint text before reaching the commits, because the picker's key handling focuses whatever element comes next. It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.

## Implementation Note
Despite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. These shortcuts only take the user to another page or open the existing commit picker, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.

# CodeRabbit settings for the CSCI 435 fork; every key is in https://docs.coderabbit.ai/reference/configuration
# Reviews treat each PR as if it were going upstream to go-gitea/gitea; where the course rules differ, they win.
language: en-US
tone_instructions: "Review like a Gitea maintainer helping a student team with little time. Raise real bugs, security holes, unmet acceptance criteria and broken repo rules. Start each comment with Required or Optional. Be brief: no praise or style nits."

reviews:

        Course rules win where they differ from upstream: PRs here are merged with a merge commit, and AI logs and .claude-students docs are committed on purpose.
        - Scope: a PR covers one issue. Flag changes unrelated to the linked issue (CONTRIBUTING.md: "Don't make changes unrelated to your PR").
        - Layers: imports flow cmd → routers → services → models → modules only. Flag an import against that direction.
        - Comments: short, explaining why, never narrating the code. Flag a removed comment that is still true. Never ask for docstrings.
        - Docs drift: if the change makes a statement in a .claude-students/docs page wrong, ask for that page to be fixed in the same PR (AGENTS.md).
        - Commits: a commit made with AI help, including one pushed by a bot, ends with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer, and no commit carries `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by` (AGENTS.md, .claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md). If possible, the message also names the person who approved the change, since a human approves every commit.
        - Skip anything `make fmt`, `make lint-go`, `make lint-js`, `make lint-css` or `make lint-templates` enforces; CI runs them.
    - path: "**/*.go"
      instructions: |
        - A new .go file starts with `// Copyright <current year> The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.` and `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`.
        - Writes that must roll back together run inside `db.WithTx` or `db.WithTx2`, and every function in the transaction takes `context.Context` first.
        - XORM: flag an `Update` or `Delete` with no `Where` or ID condition; it touches every row.
        - Before reading or changing another user's or repository's data, the doer's permission is checked. Treat a missing check as a security bug.
        - Handlers fail through the context helpers (`ctx.NotFound`, `ctx.ServerError`, `ctx.JSONError` and the like), never by writing the response by hand.
        - User-visible text is a locale key, never a literal; user-facing errors go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`.
        - `go.mod` and `go.sum` change only when the feature needs it, after `make tidy`.
    - path: "**/*_test.go"
      instructions: |
        - Prefer a unit test next to the code over an integration test when the logic can be tested alone (AGENTS.md).
        - A new test package has `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`, or its fixtures never load.
        - Cover the normal case, invalid input and permission checks where they apply (docs/sprint0/standards.md).
        - Integration tests should run in under 2 seconds. Don't ask for tests beyond what the acceptance criteria need.
    - path: "models/migrations/**"
      instructions: |
        - A new migration is appended at the bottom of the slice in `migrations.go`. Never insert in the middle, renumber, or edit a migration that is already on main.
        - It lives in `v1_27/v<id>.go` and declares its own local copy of each struct inside the function. It never imports a live model from `models/`.
        - Partial table changes use `SyncWithOptions` with `IgnoreDropIndices` and `IgnoreConstrains`, not plain `Sync`.
        - A column added to an existing table is `NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>`, so old rows are filled.
        - It has a `v<id>_test.go`, whose fixtures folder under `models/migrations/fixtures/` matches the test function name exactly.
    - path: "routers/api/v1/**"

    - path: "modules/structs/**"

    - path: "templates/**"

        - Hide and show with the `tw-hidden` class. Use `tw-` utilities and `flex-*` helpers rather than per-child margins (AGENTS.md).
        - Ids and classes are kebab-case with 2–3 feature keywords. Use `<button>` and other semantic elements rather than a clickable `<div>`.
        - User content reaches the page through the existing render and sanitiser helpers. Flag user input inserted as raw HTML as a security bug (.claude-students/docs/modules-markup.md).
    - path: "web_src/js/**"

        Follow docs/guidelines-frontend.md:
        - Use `import type` for type-only imports and `@ts-expect-error`, not `@ts-ignore`.
        - Use `!` rather than `?.` or `??` when a value always exists (AGENTS.md).
        - Mark a function `async` only when it awaits or returns a Promise. An async event listener calls `e.preventDefault()` before its first `await`.
        - Requests use the `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` wrappers from `modules/fetch.ts`. Read data attributes with `getAttribute`, not `dataset`, and never bind user-provided data directly onto DOM nodes.
        - Show and hide with `showElem`, `hideElem` and `toggleElem`; prefix custom DOM events with `ce-`.
        - Don't mix Vue with Fomantic-UI, and don't use JSX.
        - No user-visible literals: text comes from a locale key, through `data-locale-*` attributes or `window.config.i18n`.
        - New logic in a `.ts` module gets a vitest `*.test.ts` file next to it.
    - path: "web_src/css/**"
      instructions: |
        - Prefer `tw-` utilities and `flex-*` helpers; use `gt-` or `g-` helpers only when no Tailwind utility exists.
        - Avoid `!important`. Where it can't be avoided, a comment says why.
        - Add a new, prefixed class rather than restyling a Fomantic class.
        - Colours come from the theme's `var(--color-*)` variables, never a literal colour, or the other themes break (.claude-students/docs/frontend-css.md).
    - path: "docs/sprint2/diagrams/**"
      instructions: |
        Course deliverable D6 (.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md, "UML diagrams (D6)"); review it as a course submission, not as code.

    - path: "docs/sprint2/checkin/**"

It answers three questions in about 150 words each: what is done and what remains, one thing learned, one thing to do differently. Flag a missing answer or one only a sentence or two long. Do not comment on writing style.
    - path: "options/locale/**"

```text
170 web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
  registerShortcut({
    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: link,
    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

```text
Title: feat(shortcut): c shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the commit picker

Closes #59

## What changed and why

On GitHub, `c` starts a new issue or pull request from the list, and opens the commit picker on a pull request's changed files. Gitea had no such shortcut. Building on #56's registry and #58's link shortcuts, this PR adds `c` in those three places.

- **The create buttons declare `c` themselves.** "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are links, so they declare `c` the same way #58's tabs declare their `g` shortcuts, and `c` goes where the button leads, exactly as a click would. When the repository uses issue templates, that is the template chooser.
- **Only a button that really creates something declares it.** An archived repository has no create button, and its pull request list shows "Compare commits" in that place; a "New Pull Request" button the user can't use is greyed out. The list page already decides all of this, so in each of these cases `c` simply doesn't exist.
- **The commit picker declares `c` itself.** It is a Vue component that builds its own button, so it adds `c` when it appears on the "Files changed" tab. `c` opens it the same way a click does, with focus on its first entry, and never closes it.
- **Each `c` is listed with what it opens** ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab, using existing strings, so nothing new needs translating.
- The docs in `.claude-students` describe how a component adds its own shortcut.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** `c` on the issue list goes where "New Issue" leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser.
- **AC2:** `c` on the pull request list goes where "New Pull Request" leads.
- **AC3:** a greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, and an archived repository's lists, declare no `c`, so it does nothing.
- **AC4:** on the "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the commit picker with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click.
- **AC5:** `c` only exists on those three pages, so it does nothing elsewhere; when `c` is the second key of `g c`, only `g c` runs.
- **AC6:** each `c` is described by what it opens, under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

Almost all of this PR is wiring: which button declares `c` is decided by the list page, and the commit picker only exists on a real pull request. So the tests are Playwright tests on real pages.

- **No new unit tests, and why.** The only new code is a two-line action in the commit picker. #58's unit tests already cover a link turning into a shortcut, and the registry's handling of `c` inside `g c` is covered by #56's. A unit test of the picker would have to fake its loading of the commits and its focus handling, so it would mostly test the fakes.
- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** Each of the 3 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the situation where a mistake would show. A signed-in user, because only then is "New Pull Request" usable. A signed-out visitor and an archived repository, the only times the button is greyed out or replaced by "Compare commits", which looks the same as the create button to the page code. A real pull request's "Files changed" tab, the only place the picker exists and the only way to see where focus lands.
- **What "nothing happens" means here.** For AC3 the tests check that the page declares no `c`, instead of pressing `c` and waiting to see that nothing happened. Showing that a key didn't start a navigation races with whatever is pressed next, and whether `c` exists is decided by the declaration alone.

**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real: declaring `c` on the greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, declaring it on "Compare commits" in an archived repository, removing it from "New Issue", and letting `c` close an open picker. Each break failed the matching test, and #56's and #58's tests stayed green.

**Not covered automatically, and why.** The template chooser isn't driven separately: "New Issue" links to it itself, and `c` goes wherever that link points. `c` doing nothing on an issue's own page, the compare page and a pull request's conversation tab was checked by hand, since there is no picker or create button there to declare it.

**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: both lists signed in and out, an archived repository, and a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, where `c` and a mouse click gave the same focus steps through the arrow keys.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | On the issue list, `c` goes to the new issue page |
| AC2 | On the pull request list, `c` goes where "New Pull Request" leads |
| AC3 | Signed out, the greyed-out "New Pull Request" declares no `c`; in an archived repository neither list declares `c`, though "Compare commits" is shown |
| AC4 | On a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the picker with focus on its first entry, `c` again leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to its button |
| AC5 | On the issue list, `g c` goes to the front page instead of starting a new issue |
| AC6 | "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are in "Issues"; the picker's section is "Pull Requests" |

## CI / manual verification

- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.
- `make test-frontend`: 361 tests pass.
- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.
- The 10 Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` pass locally on Chromium and Firefox; each new one runs in under 1.5 s.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` reports only the two `models-issues.md` size limits, which were failing before this PR.

## Design

Design decisions noted under issue #59.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- None.

**Encountered:**
- In the commit picker on "Files changed", ArrowDown from the first entry stops on the "hold Shift for a range" hint text before reaching the commits, because the picker's key handling focuses whatever element comes next. It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.

## Implementation Note
Despite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. These shortcuts only take the user to another page or open the existing commit picker, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes, and ran the headless-browser checks and the checks that each test fails when its code is broken. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. AI-Log reference under related Issue #59.

```text
<script lang="ts">
import {defineComponent} from 'vue';
import {SvgIcon} from '../svg.ts';
import {GET} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {generateElemId} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {registerShortcut} from '../modules/shortcut.ts';

type Commit = {
  id: string,
  hovered: boolean,
  selected: boolean,
  summary: string,
  committer_or_author_name: string,
  time: string,
  short_sha: string,
}

type CommitListResult = {
  commits: Array<Commit>,
  last_review_commit_sha: string,
  locale: Record<string, string>,
}

export default defineComponent({
  components: {SvgIcon},
  data: () => {
    const el = document.querySelector('#diff-commit-select')!;
    return {
      menuVisible: false,
      isLoading: false,
      queryParams: el.getAttribute('data-queryparams'),
      issueLink: el.getAttribute('data-issuelink'),
      locale: {
        filter_changes_by_commit: el.getAttribute('data-filter_changes_by_commit'),
      } as Record<string, string>,
      mergeBase: el.getAttribute('data-merge-base'),
      shortcutSection: el.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section'),
      commits: [] as Array<Commit>,
      hoverActivated: false,
      lastReviewCommitSha: '' as string | null,
      uniqueIdMenu: generateElemId('diff-commit-selector-menu-'),
      uniqueIdShowAll: generateElemId('diff-commit-selector-show-all-'),
    };
  },
  computed: {
    commitsSinceLastReview() {
      if (this.lastReviewCommitSha) {
        return this.commits.length - this.commits.findIndex((x) => x.id === this.lastReviewCommitSha) - 1;
      }
      return 0;
    },
  },
  mounted() {
    document.body.addEventListener('click', this.onBodyClick);
    this.$el.addEventListener('keydown', this.onKeyDown);
    this.$el.addEventListener('keyup', this.onKeyUp);
    registerShortcut({
      keys: 'c',
      description: this.locale.filter_changes_by_commit,
      section: this.shortcutSection ?? undefined,
      element: this.$el,
      action: () => {
        if (!this.menuVisible) this.toggleMenu(); // opens like a click, but never closes an open menu
      },
    });
  },
  unmounted() {
    document.body.removeEventListener('click', this.onBodyClick);
    this.$el.removeEventListener('keydown', this.onKeyDown);
    this.$el.removeEventListener('keyup', this.onKeyUp);
  },
  methods: {
    onBodyClick(event: MouseEvent) {
      // close this menu on click outside of this element when the dropdown is currently visible opened
      if (this.$el.contains(event.target)) return;
      if (this.menuVisible) {
        this.toggleMenu();
      }
    },
    onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (!this.menuVisible) return;
      const item = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      if (!this.$el.contains(item)) return;
      switch (event.key) {
        case 'ArrowDown': // select next element
          event.preventDefault();
          this.focusElem(item.nextElementSibling as HTMLElement, item);
          break;
        case 'ArrowUp': // select previous element
          event.preventDefault();
          this.focusElem(item.previousElementSibling as HTMLElement, item);
          break;
        case 'Escape': // close menu
          event.preventDefault();
          item.tabIndex = -1;
          this.toggleMenu();
          break;
      }
      if (event.key === 'ArrowDown' || event.key === 'ArrowUp') {
        const item = document.activeElement; // try to highlight the selected commits
        const commitIdx = item?.matches('.item') ? item.getAttribute('data-commit-idx') : null;
        if (commitIdx) this.highlight(this.commits[Number(commitIdx)]);
      }
    },
    onKeyUp(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (!this.menuVisible) return;
      const item = document.activeElement;
      if (!this.$el.contains(item)) return;
      if (event.key === 'Shift' && this.hoverActivated) {
        // shift is not pressed anymore -> deactivate hovering and reset hovered and selected
        this.hoverActivated = false;
        for (const commit of this.commits) {
          commit.hovered = false;
          commit.selected = false;
        }
      }
    },
    highlight(commit: Commit) {
      if (!this.hoverActivated) return;
      const indexSelected = this.commits.findIndex((x) => x.selected);
      const indexCurrentElem = this.commits.findIndex((x) => x.id === commit.id);

```text
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
  registerShortcut({
    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: link,
    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

```text
## Design Decisions - @ab-wm

### Decisions for Commit 1
#### Decision 1: The create button's link in the list declares `c`, and only when it really creates something

**Decision:** On the issue and pull request lists, the "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" buttons declare `c` in the page's HTML, the same way the tabs declare their `g` shortcuts (#58).
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The page code finds the create button and clicks it. (b) The server hands the page the address of the create page.
**Rationale:** The list page already decides which button to show in the context of this page (archived repository, permissions, etc.). Declaring the shortcut on the button follows those decisions, so AC3 and AC5 need no rules of their own. (a) would have to tell the create button apart from "Compare commits", which looks the same to the page code, and check for the greyed-out state, repeating what the page already knows. (b) would repeat the same rules in a second place, where they could drift apart. Nothing else happens when the buttons are clicked, so going where the button leads is the same as clicking it (AC1, AC2).
**Consequences:** No new page code: the buttons reuse #58's way of declaring a shortcut on a link, so #59 builds on #58. A greyed-out "New Pull Request" button still has an address, so the page must leave it undeclared, or `c` would go where a click can't.

### Decisions for Commit 2
#### Decision 2: The commit picker declares `c` itself, and `c` only ever opens it

**Decision:** The commit picker on the "Files changed" tab adds its own `c` shortcut when it appears on the page. Pressing `c` opens the picker the same way a click does, and does nothing when it is already open.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A new general attribute in the page's HTML that makes a shortcut click an element, like the one #58 added for links. (b) The page code that sets up the picker adds `c` from outside and clicks the picker's button.
**Rationale:** The picker's button is built by the picker itself after the page loads, and a click opens or closes it. Only the picker knows whether it is open, and it already has its translated label ("Filter by commit"). Declaring `c` inside the picker lets `c` open it through the same steps a click takes, so the first entry gets focus and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click (AC4), without ever closing it by accident. (a) would add a general mechanism for a single use, would have to reach inside the picker for a button that doesn't exist until the picker is built, and a click would close an open picker. (b) has the same closing problem and depends on the picker's inner markup from outside it.
**Consequences:** `c` only exists while the picker is on the page, so it is missing on the compare page and on an issue's own page (AC5). The picker gets its section ("Pull Requests", an existing string) from the page, the same way the "Go to file" box got its section in #56. This is the first shortcut a component adds from its own code instead of from the page's HTML.

   191	     * When a commit is clicked while holding Shift, it enables range selection.
   192	     * - The range selection is a half-open, half-closed range, meaning it excludes the start commit but includes the end commit.
   193	     * - The start of the commit range is always the previous commit of the first clicked commit.
   194	     * - If the first commit in the list is clicked, the mergeBase will be used as the start of the range instead.
   195	     * - The second Shift-click defines the end of the range.
   196	     * - Once both are selected, the diff view for the selected commit range will open.
   197	     */
   198	    commitClickedShift(commit: Commit) {
   199	      this.hoverActivated = !this.hoverActivated;
   200	      commit.selected = true;
   201	      // Second click -> determine our range and open links accordingly
   202	      if (!this.hoverActivated) {
   203	        // since at least one commit is selected, we can determine the range
   204	        // find all selected commits and generate a link
   205	        const firstSelected = this.commits.findIndex((x) => x.selected);
   206	        const lastSelected = this.commits.findLastIndex((x) => x.selected);
   207	        let beforeCommitID: string | null = null;
   208	        if (firstSelected === 0) {
   209	          beforeCommitID = this.mergeBase;
   210	        } else {
   211	          beforeCommitID = this.commits[firstSelected - 1].id;
   212	        }
   213	        const afterCommitID = this.commits[lastSelected].id;
   214
   215	        if (firstSelected === lastSelected) {
   216	          // if the start and end are the same, we show this single commit
   217	          window.location.assign(`${this.issueLink}/commits/${afterCommitID}${this.queryParams}`);
   218	        } else if (beforeCommitID === this.mergeBase && afterCommitID === this.commits.at(-1)!.id) {
   219	          // if the first commit is selected and the last commit is selected, we show all commits
   220	          window.location.assign(`${this.issueLink}/files${this.queryParams}`);
   221	        } else {
   222	          window.location.assign(`${this.issueLink}/files/${beforeCommitID}..${afterCommitID}${this.queryParams}`);
   223	        }
   224	      }
   225	    },
   226	  },
   227	});
   228	</script>

async function createRepo(page: Page) {

// PullRequestContext contains context information for making a new pull request
type PullRequestContext struct {
	ctx *Context

	baseRepo, headRepo *repo_model.Repository

	canCreateNewPull    *bool
	defaultTargetBranch *string
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) SameRepo() bool {
	return prc.baseRepo != nil && prc.headRepo != nil && prc.baseRepo.ID == prc.headRepo.ID
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) CanCreateNewPull() bool {
	if prc.canCreateNewPull != nil {
		return *prc.canCreateNewPull
	}
	ctx := prc.ctx
	// People who have push access or have forked repository can propose a new pull request.
	can := prc.baseRepo.CanContentChange() &&
		(ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWrite(unit_model.TypeCode) || (ctx.IsSigned && repo_model.HasForkedRepo(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID)))
	prc.canCreateNewPull = &can
	return can
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) MakeDefaultCompareLink(headBranch string) string {
	return prc.baseRepo.Link() + "/compare/" +
		util.PathEscapeSegments(prc.DefaultTargetBranch()) + "..." +
		util.Iif(prc.SameRepo(), "", util.PathEscapeSegments(prc.headRepo.OwnerName)+":") +
		util.PathEscapeSegments(headBranch)
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) DefaultTargetBranch() string {
	if prc.defaultTargetBranch != nil {
		return *prc.defaultTargetBranch
	}
	branchName := prc.baseRepo.GetPullRequestTargetBranch(prc.ctx)
	prc.defaultTargetBranch = &branchName
	return branchName
}

// Repository contains information to operate a repository
type Repository struct {
	Permission access_model.Permission

	Repository *repo_model.Repository
	Owner      *user_model.User

	RepoLink string
	GitRepo  *git.Repository

	// People who have push access or have forked repository can propose a new pull request.
	can := prc.baseRepo.CanContentChange() &&
		(ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWrite(unit_model.TypeCode) || (ctx.IsSigned && repo_model.HasForkedRepo(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID)))
	prc.canCreateNewPull = &can
	return can
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) MakeDefaultCompareLink(headBranch string) string {
	return prc.baseRepo.Link() + "/compare/" +
		util.PathEscapeSegments(prc.DefaultTargetBranch()) + "..." +
		util.Iif(prc.SameRepo(), "", util.PathEscapeSegments(prc.headRepo.OwnerName)+":") +
		util.PathEscapeSegments(headBranch)
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) DefaultTargetBranch() string {
	if prc.defaultTargetBranch != nil {
		return *prc.defaultTargetBranch
	}
	branchName := prc.baseRepo.GetPullRequestTargetBranch(prc.ctx)
	prc.defaultTargetBranch = &branchName
	return branchName
}
```

## Gotchas
  if (!el) return;
  createApp(RepoContributors, {repoLink: el.getAttribute('data-repo-link')}).mount(el);
  ```

  So adding a component always means touching `frontend-js.md`'s wiring too.
- Props come from `data-*` attributes read with `getAttribute`, or from `window.config.pageData`
  (set by the handler via `ctx.PageData`, see `templates.md`). Do not fetch configuration the
  server could have handed you.
- Show and hide with `v-if` / `v-show` — not `.tw-hidden`, which is the plain-JS mechanism.
- **Do not mix Vue with Fomantic-UI JavaScript.** Fomantic's CSS classes are fine; its jQuery
  behaviours fight Vue's ownership of the DOM.
- No JSX — SFCs only.
- Data fetching still goes through `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`.
- Logic worth testing is pulled into a sibling `.ts` file and tested there; the `.vue` file stays
  presentational. `ActionRunView.ts` beside `RepoActionView.vue` is the pattern.

## Recipes

**Add a component.** Create `YourThing.vue`, a mount block in the owning `features/` module,
a root element with the data attributes it needs in the template, and — if it has real logic — a
sibling `.ts` with a `.test.ts`.

**Give a component server data.** Small values as `data-*` attributes on the mount point; anything
structured via `ctx.PageData` in the handler, read as `window.config.pageData`.

**Give a component a keyboard shortcut.** Call `registerShortcut` (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`)
in `mounted()` with `element: this.$el`, so it lives exactly as long as the component, and let the
action use the component's own state: `web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.vue` opens its menu
on `c` but never closes it. A translated section arrives as `data-shortcut-section` on the mount point.

**Test one.** `pnpm exec vitest <name>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A component with no mount call is dead code that still ships in the bundle — the compiler will
  not tell you.
- `.ts` files in this directory are not components; they are stores and extracted logic. Do not
  assume everything here is a `.vue`.
- Because mounting is element-guarded, a typo in the root element's id or class fails silently:
  nothing renders and nothing errors.

```text
**Read when:** building or changing an interactive widget complex enough to need state.
**Not here:** how a component gets mounted -> `frontend-js.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`.

## Responsibilities

Vue 3 single-file components for the parts of the UI too stateful for a Go template plus a little
JavaScript: the Actions run viewer, the diff file tree, the dashboard repo list, the merge form,
the various repo charts.

`docs/guidelines-frontend.md` draws the line as: **Go templates for simple and SEO-relevant pages,
Vue for complex interactive pages.** A page that only needs a toggle does not need Vue.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/components/RepoActionView.vue` | the Actions run log viewer |
| `web_src/js/components/DiffFileTree.vue`, `DiffFileTreeItem.vue` | the code-review file tree |
| `web_src/js/components/PullRequestMergeForm.vue` | the merge button and its options |
| `web_src/js/components/DashboardRepoList.vue` | the dashboard repo list |
| `web_src/js/components/ViewFileTreeStore.ts` | a plain-TS store shared by the file-tree components |
| `web_src/js/components/ActionRunView.ts`, `WorkflowGraph.utils.ts` | logic extracted out of the neighbouring `.vue` files so it is unit-testable |
| `web_src/js/components/*.test.ts` | Vitest tests, colocated |

## Conventions & invariants

- Filenames are PascalCase and match the component name.
- **Components do not mount themselves.** A `features/` module does it, guarded by the presence of
  its root element:
```
</details></tool-use>

<script lang="ts">
import {defineComponent} from 'vue';
import {SvgIcon} from '../svg.ts';
import {GET} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {generateElemId} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {registerShortcut} from '../modules/shortcut.ts';

type Commit = {
  id: string,
  hovered: boolean,
  selected: boolean,
  summary: string,
  committer_or_author_name: string,
  time: string,
  short_sha: string,
}

type CommitListResult = {
  commits: Array<Commit>,
  last_review_commit_sha: string,
  locale: Record<string, string>,
}

export default defineComponent({
  components: {SvgIcon},
  data: () => {
    const el = document.querySelector('#diff-commit-select')!;
    return {
      menuVisible: false,
      isLoading: false,
      queryParams: el.getAttribute('data-queryparams'),
      issueLink: el.getAttribute('data-issuelink'),
      locale: {
        filter_changes_by_commit: el.getAttribute('data-filter_changes_by_commit'),
      } as Record<string, string>,
      mergeBase: el.getAttribute('data-merge-base'),
      shortcutSection: el.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section'),
      commits: [] as Array<Commit>,
      hoverActivated: false,
      lastReviewCommitSha: '' as string | null,
      uniqueIdMenu: generateElemId('diff-commit-selector-menu-'),
      uniqueIdShowAll: generateElemId('diff-commit-selector-show-all-'),
    };
  },
  computed: {
    commitsSinceLastReview() {
      if (this.lastReviewCommitSha) {
        return this.commits.length - this.commits.findIndex((x) => x.id === this.lastReviewCommitSha) - 1;
      }
      return 0;
    },
  },
  mounted() {
    document.body.addEventListener('click', this.onBodyClick);
    this.$el.addEventListener('keydown', this.onKeyDown);
    this.$el.addEventListener('keyup', this.onKeyUp);
    registerShortcut({
      keys: 'c',
      description: this.locale.filter_changes_by_commit,
      section: this.shortcutSection ?? undefined,
      element: this.$el,
      action: () => {
        if (!this.menuVisible) this.toggleMenu(); // opens like a click, but never closes an open menu
      },
    });
  },
  unmounted() {
    document.body.removeEventListener('click', this.onBodyClick);
    this.$el.removeEventListener('keydown', this.onKeyDown);
    this.$el.removeEventListener('keyup', this.onKeyUp);
  },
  methods: {
    onBodyClick(event: MouseEvent) {
      // close this menu on click outside of this element when the dropdown is currently visible opened
      if (this.$el.contains(event.target)) return;
      if (this.menuVisible) {
        this.toggleMenu();
      }
    },
    onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (!this.menuVisible) return;
      const item = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      if (!this.$el.contains(item)) return;
      switch (event.key) {
        case 'ArrowDown': // select next element
          event.preventDefault();
          this.focusElem(item.nextElementSibling as HTMLElement, item);
          break;
        case 'ArrowUp': // select previous element
          event.preventDefault();
          this.focusElem(item.previousElementSibling as HTMLElement, item);
          break;
        case 'Escape': // close menu
          event.preventDefault();
          item.tabIndex = -1;
          this.toggleMenu();
          break;
      }
      if (event.key === 'ArrowDown' || event.key === 'ArrowUp') {
        const item = document.activeElement; // try to highlight the selected commits
        const commitIdx = item?.matches('.item') ? item.getAttribute('data-commit-idx') : null;
        if (commitIdx) this.highlight(this.commits[Number(commitIdx)]);
      }
    },
    onKeyUp(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (!this.menuVisible) return;
      const item = document.activeElement;
      if (!this.$el.contains(item)) return;
      if (event.key === 'Shift' && this.hoverActivated) {
        // shift is not pressed anymore -> deactivate hovering and reset hovered and selected
        this.hoverActivated = false;
        for (const commit of this.commits) {
          commit.hovered = false;
          commit.selected = false;

      }

      const indexCurrentElem = this.commits.findIndex((x) => x.id === commit.id);
      for (const [idx, commit] of this.commits.entries()) {
        commit.hovered = Math.min(indexSelected, indexCurrentElem) <= idx && idx <= Math.max(indexSelected, indexCurrentElem);
      }
    },

        elem.focus();
      }

      if (!this.commits.length && this.menuVisible && !this.isLoading) {

sim-59
Title: feat(shortcut): c shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the commit picker

Closes #59

## What changed and why

On GitHub, `c` starts a new issue or pull request from the list, and opens the commit picker on a pull request's changed files. Gitea had no such shortcut. Building on #56's registry and #58's link shortcuts, this PR adds `c` in those three places.

- **The create buttons declare `c` themselves.** "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are links, so they declare `c` the same way #58's tabs declare their `g` shortcuts, and `c` goes where the button leads, exactly as a click would. When the repository uses issue templates, that is the template chooser.
- **Only a button that really creates something declares it.** An archived repository has no create button, and its pull request list shows "Compare commits" in that place; a "New Pull Request" button the user can't use is greyed out. The list page already decides all of this, so in each of these cases `c` simply doesn't exist.
- **The commit picker declares `c` itself.** It is a Vue component that builds its own button, so it adds `c` when it appears on the "Files changed" tab. `c` opens it the same way a click does, with focus on its first entry, and never closes it.
- **Each `c` is listed with what it opens** ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab, using existing strings, so nothing new needs translating.
- The docs in `.claude-students` describe how a component adds its own shortcut.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** `c` on the issue list goes where "New Issue" leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser.
- **AC2:** `c` on the pull request list goes where "New Pull Request" leads.
- **AC3:** a greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, and an archived repository's lists, declare no `c`, so it does nothing.
- **AC4:** on the "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the commit picker with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click.
- **AC5:** `c` only exists on those three pages, so it does nothing elsewhere; when `c` is the second key of `g c`, only `g c` runs.
- **AC6:** each `c` is described by what it opens, under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

Almost all of this PR is wiring: which button declares `c` is decided by the list page, and the commit picker only exists on a real pull request. So the tests are Playwright tests on real pages.

- **No new unit tests, and why.** The only new code is a two-line action in the commit picker. #58's unit tests already cover a link turning into a shortcut, and the registry's handling of `c` inside `g c` is covered by #56's. A unit test of the picker would have to fake its loading of the commits and its focus handling, so it would mostly test the fakes.
- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** Each of the 3 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the situation where a mistake would show. A signed-in user, because only then is "New Pull Request" usable. A signed-out visitor and an archived repository, the only times the button is greyed out or replaced by "Compare commits", which looks the same as the create button to the page code. A real pull request's "Files changed" tab, the only place the picker exists and the only way to see where focus lands.
- **What "nothing happens" means here.** For AC3 the tests check that the page declares no `c`, instead of pressing `c` and waiting to see that nothing happened. Showing that a key didn't start a navigation races with whatever is pressed next, and whether `c` exists is decided by the declaration alone.

**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real: declaring `c` on the greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, declaring it on "Compare commits" in an archived repository, removing it from "New Issue", and letting `c` close an open picker. Each break failed the matching test, and #56's and #58's tests stayed green.

**Not covered automatically, and why.** The template chooser isn't driven separately: "New Issue" links to it itself, and `c` goes wherever that link points. `c` doing nothing on an issue's own page, the compare page and a pull request's conversation tab was checked by hand, since there is no picker or create button there to declare it.

**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: both lists signed in and out, an archived repository, and a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, where `c` and a mouse click gave the same focus steps through the arrow keys.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | On the issue list, `c` goes to the new issue page |
| AC2 | On the pull request list, `c` goes where "New Pull Request" leads |
| AC3 | Signed out, the greyed-out "New Pull Request" declares no `c`; in an archived repository neither list declares `c`, though "Compare commits" is shown |
| AC4 | On a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the picker with focus on its first entry, `c` again leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to its button |
| AC5 | On the issue list, `g c` goes to the front page instead of starting a new issue |
| AC6 | "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are in "Issues"; the picker's section is "Pull Requests" |

## CI / manual verification

- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.
- `make test-frontend`: 361 tests pass.
- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.
- The 10 Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` pass locally on Chromium and Firefox; each new one runs in under 1.5 s.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` reports only the two `models-issues.md` size limits, which were failing before this PR.

## Design

Design decisions noted under issue #59.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- None.

**Encountered:**
- In the commit picker on "Files changed", ArrowDown from the first entry stops on the "hold Shift for a range" hint text before reaching the commits, because the picker's key handling focuses whatever element comes next. It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.

## Implementation Note
Despite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. These shortcuts only take the user to another page or open the existing commit picker, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes, and ran the headless-browser checks and the checks that each test fails when its code is broken. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. AI-Log reference under related Issue #59.
