import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

        The project rules are AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/sprint0/standards.md, docs/guidelines-backend.md, docs/guidelines-frontend.md, and the .claude-students/docs page that .claude-students/INDEX.md maps to the changed path. Cite the rule when you raise one.
        Course rules win where they differ from upstream: PRs here are merged with a merge commit, and AI logs and .claude-students docs are committed on purpose.
        - Scope: a PR covers one issue. Flag changes unrelated to the linked issue (CONTRIBUTING.md: "Don't make changes unrelated to your PR").
        - Layers: imports flow cmd → routers → services → models → modules only. Flag an import against that direction.
        - Comments: short, explaining why, never narrating the code. Flag a removed comment that is still true. Never ask for docstrings.
        - Docs drift: if the change makes a statement in a .claude-students/docs page wrong, ask for that page to be fixed in the same PR (AGENTS.md).
        - Commits: a commit made with AI help, including one pushed by a bot, ends with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer, and no commit carries `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by` (AGENTS.md, .claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md). If possible, the message also names the person who approved the change, since a human approves every commit.
        - Skip anything `make fmt`, `make lint-go`, `make lint-js`, `make lint-css` or `make lint-templates` enforces; CI runs them.
    - path: "**/*.go"
      instructions: |
        - A new .go file starts with `// Copyright <current year> The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.` and `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`.
        - Writes that must roll back together run inside `db.WithTx` or `db.WithTx2`, and every function in the transaction takes `context.Context` first.
        - XORM: flag an `Update` or `Delete` with no `Where` or ID condition; it touches every row.
        - Before reading or changing another user's or repository's data, the doer's permission is checked. Treat a missing check as a security bug.
        - Handlers fail through the context helpers (`ctx.NotFound`, `ctx.ServerError`, `ctx.JSONError` and the like), never by writing the response by hand.
        - User-visible text is a locale key, never a literal; user-facing errors go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`.

The review is done: 3 agents, about **270k tokens**. The skeptic confirmed 7 problems and rated 2 more plausible; none were refuted. (The journal stores findings in a different order from the verdicts, so I matched them up by content.) After merging duplicates, there are 8 real items:

**Code: 2 items**
1. **`c` doesn't move focus the way a click does.** A click leaves focus on the picker's button. `c` leaves it on the page until the commits finish loading, so Escape and the arrow keys do nothing while it loads. If loading fails, the menu stays stuck open, `c` won't close it, and only the mouse can. That breaks AC4's "as after clicking". Fix: focus the button first, then open.
2. **`this.shortcutSection ?? undefined`** handles a null that can't happen, because `box.tmpl` always renders the attribute. AGENTS.md says to use `!` in that case, and `RepoFileSearch.vue` already treats its section as required.

**Tests: 4 items**
3. **The picker's AC6 isn't tested.** The e2e test reads the template's attribute, never what the component registers. Removing `section:` or changing `description:` keeps everything green. My "no unit tests" reasoning was wrong here: listing the shortcut needs no fake data, only a mounted component.
4. **The New Pull Request link's section isn't asserted** (`shortcut.test.ts:155`), although the PR's AC6 row claims it is.
5. **Two locators check implementation details.** `.issue-list-new` is on both buttons, so it doesn't prove "Compare commits" is shown. The generated-id prefix for the first entry is the other one. Role-and-name locators read better and test what the user sees. That's the same kind of thing as your teammate's `tw-hidden` comment on #96.
6. **AC4 names the arrow keys**, but the test never presses one. That's plausible rather than certain, and it's a one-line fix.

**Written claims: 1 item**
7. **Two statements in the PR's test strategy are false:**
   - "the only times the button is greyed out". Mirrors and signed-in users without write access or a fork get it too.
   - "Compare commits looks the same as the create button to the page code". Only the create link has `new-pr-button`; they just share `issue-list-new`.

   The second statement also appears in your Decision 1, so it needs fixing in both decision files.

**Not worth acting on: 1 item**
8. The commits don't name who approved them. The rule says "if possible", and you are both the author and the approver.

I'll start with item 1, since it's real behaviour, and prove it before and after by holding up the commit loading in a headless browser. Making the code change and rebuilding:

```text
1	Title: feat(shortcut): c shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the commit picker
2
3	Closes #59
4
5	## What changed and why
6
7	On GitHub, `c` starts a new issue or pull request from the list, and opens the commit picker on a pull request's changed files. Gitea had no such shortcut. Building on #56's registry and #58's link shortcuts, this PR adds `c` in those three places.
8
9	- **The create buttons declare `c` themselves.** "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are links, so they declare `c` the same way #58's tabs declare their `g` shortcuts, and `c` goes where the button leads, exactly as a click would. When the repository uses issue templates, that is the template chooser.
10	- **Only a button that really creates something declares it.** An archived repository has no create button, and its pull request list shows "Compare commits" in that place; a "New Pull Request" button the user can't use is greyed out. The list page already decides all of this, so in each of these cases `c` simply doesn't exist.
11	- **The commit picker declares `c` itself.** It is a Vue component that builds its own button, so it adds `c` when it appears on the "Files changed" tab. `c` opens it the same way a click does: focus moves to the picker's button first, so Escape works even while the commits are still loading, then to its first entry. `c` never closes it.
12	- **Each `c` is listed with what it opens** ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab, using existing strings, so nothing new needs translating.
13	- The docs in `.claude-students` describe how a component adds its own shortcut.
14
15	## How the changes relate to the ACs
16
17	- **AC1:** `c` on the issue list goes where "New Issue" leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser.
18	- **AC2:** `c` on the pull request list goes where "New Pull Request" leads.
19	- **AC3:** a greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, and an archived repository's lists, declare no `c`, so it does nothing.
20	- **AC4:** on the "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the commit picker with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click.
21	- **AC5:** `c` only exists on those three pages, so it does nothing elsewhere; when `c` is the second key of `g c`, only `g c` runs.
22	- **AC6:** each `c` is described by what it opens, under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab.
23
24	## How it was tested
25
26	### Test strategy
27
28	Almost all of this PR is wiring: which button declares `c` is decided by the list page, and the commit picker only exists on a real pull request. So the tests are Playwright tests on real pages.
29
30	- **One unit test, for what a page can't show yet.** Which shortcuts the picker lists isn't visible anywhere until #57's dialog exists, so `web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.test.ts` mounts the picker and checks that it lists `c` as "Filter by commit" in "Pull Requests" (AC6). Everything else is covered by earlier unit tests: #58's for a link turning into a shortcut, and #56's for `c` inside `g c`. Opening the picker is left to Playwright, because a unit test would have to fake the loading of the commits and the focus handling, and would mostly test the fakes.
31	- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** Each of the 4 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the situation where a mistake would show. A signed-in user who can write to the repository, because only then is "New Pull Request" usable. A signed-out visitor, for whom it is greyed out, and an archived repository, where "Compare commits" takes its place and shares its `issue-list-new` class. A real pull request's "Files changed" tab, the only place the picker exists and the only way to see where focus lands, once normally and once with its commits held back, since focus only matters while they load.
32	- **What "nothing happens" means here.** For AC3 the tests check that the page declares no `c`, instead of pressing `c` and waiting to see that nothing happened. Showing that a key didn't start a navigation races with whatever is pressed next, and whether `c` exists is decided by the declaration alone.
33
34	**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real: declaring `c` on the greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, declaring it on "Compare commits" in an archived repository, removing it from "New Issue", letting `c` close an open picker, opening it without moving focus to its button first, and, for the unit test, dropping the picker's section, changing its description and not registering `c` at all. Each break failed the matching test, and #56's and #58's tests stayed green.
35
36	**Not covered automatically, and why.** The template chooser isn't driven separately: "New Issue" links to it itself, and `c` goes wherever that link points. `c` doing nothing on an issue's own page, the compare page and a pull request's conversation tab was checked by hand, since there is no picker or create button there to declare it.
37
38	**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: both lists signed in and out, an archived repository, and a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, where `c` and a mouse click gave the same focus steps through the arrow keys.
39
40	| AC | What the tests check |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| AC1 | On the issue list, `c` goes to the new issue page |
43	| AC2 | On the pull request list, `c` goes where "New Pull Request" leads |
44	| AC3 | Signed out, the greyed-out "New Pull Request" declares no `c`; in an archived repository neither list declares `c`, though "Compare commits" is shown |
45	| AC4 | On a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the picker with focus on its first entry, the arrow keys move within it, `c` again leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to its button, also while its commits are still loading |
46	| AC5 | On the issue list, `g c` goes to the front page instead of starting a new issue |
47	| AC6 | "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are in "Issues"; the mounted picker lists `c` as "Filter by commit" in "Pull Requests" |
48
49	## CI / manual verification
50
51	- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.
52	- `make test-frontend`: 362 tests pass, including the new one.
53	- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.
54	- The 11 Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` pass locally on Chromium and Firefox; each new one runs in under 1.5 s.
55	- `./.claude-students/check.sh` reports only the two `models-issues.md` size limits, which were failing before this PR.
56
57	## Design
58
59	Design decisions noted under issue #59.
60
61	## Tech Debt
62
63	**Introduced:**
64	- None.
65
66	**Encountered:**
67	- In the commit picker on "Files changed", ArrowDown from the first entry stops on the "hold Shift for a range" hint text before reaching the commits, because the picker's key handling focuses whatever element comes next. It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.
68
69	## Implementation Note
70	Despite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. These shortcuts only take the user to another page or open the existing commit picker, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.
71

I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. AI-Log reference under related Issue #59.

+  await expect(newPull).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Issues');
+  const compareLink = (await newPull.getAttribute('href'))!;
+  await goWith(page, 'c', new RegExp(`${compareLink.replaceAll('.', '\\.')}$`));
+  await assertNoJsError(page);
+});
+
+test('c is missing where there is nothing to create', async ({page}) => {
+  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
+  await page.goto(`${repoLink}/pulls`);
+  await expect(page.locator('.new-pr-button.disabled')).toBeVisible(); // signed out, so greyed out
+  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="c"]')).toHaveCount(0);
+
+  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
+  await apiEditRepo(page.request, owner, repoName, {archived: true});
+  await page.goto(`${repoLink}/issues`);
+  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="c"]')).toHaveCount(0);
+  await page.goto(`${repoLink}/pulls`);
+  await expect(page.getByRole('link', {name: 'Compare commits'})).toBeVisible(); // in the create button's place
+  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="c"]')).toHaveCount(0);
+  await assertNoJsError(page);
+});
+
+// a pull request with one commit; returns its "Files changed" tab
+async function createPullRequest(page: Page) {
+  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
+  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
+  await apiCreateFile(page.request, owner, repoName, 'feature.txt', 'feature', {newBranch: 'feature'});
+  const index = await apiCreatePR(page.request, owner, repoName, 'feature', 'main', 'picker');
+  return `${repoLink}/pulls/${index}/files`;
+}
+
+test('c opens the commit picker on the files changed tab', async ({page}) => {
+  await page.goto(await createPullRequest(page));
+  await expect(page.locator('#diff-commit-select')).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Pull Requests');
+  const button = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Filter by commit'});
+  const menu = page.locator('.diff-commit-selector .menu');
+  const showAll = page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: /^Show all commits/});
+  await expect(button).toBeVisible(); // the picker has mounted and declared c
+
+  await page.keyboard.press('c');
+  await expect(menu).toBeVisible();
+  await expect(showAll).toBeFocused(); // as after a click
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
+  await expect(showAll).not.toBeFocused();
+  await expect(menu.locator(':focus')).toHaveCount(1); // the arrow keys move within the menu
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');
+  await expect(showAll).toBeFocused();
+  await page.keyboard.press('c');
+  await expect(menu).toBeVisible(); // c never closes it
+  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
+  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
+  await expect(button).toBeFocused();
+  await assertNoJsError(page);
+});
+
+test('Escape closes the commit picker that c opened while its commits load', async ({page}) => {
+  let release!: () => void;
+  const held = new Promise<void>((resolve) => release = resolve);
+  await page.route('**/commits/list', async (route) => {
+    await held;
+    await route.continue();
+  });
+  await page.goto(await createPullRequest(page));
+  const menu = page.locator('.diff-commit-selector .menu');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Filter by commit'})).toBeVisible();
+
+  await page.keyboard.press('c');
+  await expect(menu.locator('.is-loading')).toBeVisible(); // the commits are still on their way
+  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
+  await expect(menu).toBeHidden(); // as after a click, which leaves focus on the button
+  release();
+  await assertNoJsError(page);
+});

160:## Pull request format
161-
162-Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
163-`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:
164-
165-1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
166-2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
167-3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.

169-   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
170-   needs a new or updated test.

     4	const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence
     5
     6	export type Shortcut = {
     7	  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
     8	  description: string, // translated
     9	  section?: string, // translated
    10	  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
    11	  action: () => void,
    12	};
    13
    14	export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;
    15
    16	function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
    17	  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
    18	}
    19
    20	// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
    21	function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
    22	  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    23	    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    24	    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
    25	  }
    26	  return null;
    27	}
    28
    29	export class ShortcutRegistry {
    30	  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
    31	  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
    32	  private pendingTime = 0;
    33
    34	  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    35	    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    36	    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    37	    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    38	    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    39	    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    40	    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
    41	  }
    42
    43	  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    44	    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
    45	  }
    46
    47	  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    48	    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    49	    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    50	    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
    51	      this.pendingKeys = '';
    52	      return;
    53	    }
    54	    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    55	    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence
    56
    57	    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    58	    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    59	    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    60	    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    61	    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    62	    if (!match && keys !== key) {
    63	      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
    64	      keys = key;
    65	      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    66	    }
    67	    this.pendingKeys = '';
    68	    if (!match) return;
    69
    70	    e.preventDefault();
    71	    if (match === 'prefix') {
    72	      this.pendingKeys = keys;
    73	      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    74	    } else {
    75	      match.action();
    76	    }
    77	  }

```text
## Design Decisions - @ab-wm

### Decisions for Commit 1
#### Decision 1: The create button's link in the list declares `c`, and only when it really creates something

**Decision:** On the issue and pull request lists, the "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" buttons declare `c` in the page's HTML, the same way the tabs declare their `g` shortcuts (#58).
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The page code finds the create button and clicks it. (b) The server hands the page the address of the create page.
**Rationale:** The list page already decides which button to show in the context of this page (archived repository, permissions, etc.). Declaring the shortcut on the button follows those decisions, so AC3 and AC5 need no rules of their own. (a) would have to tell the create button apart from "Compare commits", which shares its `issue-list-new` class, and check for the greyed-out state, repeating what the page already knows. (b) would repeat the same rules in a second place, where they could drift apart. Nothing else happens when the buttons are clicked, so going where the button leads is the same as clicking it (AC1, AC2).
**Consequences:** No new page code: the buttons reuse #58's way of declaring a shortcut on a link, so #59 builds on #58. A greyed-out "New Pull Request" button still has an address, so the page must leave it undeclared, or `c` would go where a click can't.

### Decisions for Commit 2
#### Decision 2: The commit picker declares `c` itself, and `c` only ever opens it

**Decision:** The commit picker on the "Files changed" tab adds its own `c` shortcut when it appears on the page. Pressing `c` opens the picker the same way a click does, and does nothing when it is already open.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A new general attribute in the page's HTML that makes a shortcut click an element, like the one #58 added for links. (b) The page code that sets up the picker adds `c` from outside and clicks the picker's button.
**Rationale:** The picker's button is built by the picker itself after the page loads, and a click opens or closes it. Only the picker knows whether it is open, and it already has its translated label ("Filter by commit"). Declaring `c` inside the picker lets `c` open it through the same steps a click takes, so the first entry gets focus and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click (AC4), without ever closing it by accident. (a) would add a general mechanism for a single use, would have to reach inside the picker for a button that doesn't exist until the picker is built, and a click would close an open picker. (b) has the same closing problem and depends on the picker's inner markup from outside it.
**Consequences:** `c` only exists while the picker is on the page, so it is missing on the compare page and on an issue's own page (AC5). The picker gets its section ("Pull Requests", an existing string) from the page, the same way the "Go to file" box got its section in #56. This is the first shortcut a component adds from its own code instead of from the page's HTML.
-----
## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- None so far.

**Encountered:**
- In the commit picker on "Files changed", ArrowDown from the first entry stops on the "hold Shift for a range" hint text before reaching the commits, because the picker's key handling focuses whatever element comes next (`web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.vue`, `onKeyDown` / `focusElem`). It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.
```

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
```

    onBodyClick(event: MouseEvent) {

    onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (!this.menuVisible) return;
      const item = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      if (!this.$el.contains(item)) return;
      switch (event.key) {
        case 'ArrowDown': // select next element
          event.preventDefault();
          this.focusElem(item.nextElementSibling as HTMLElement, item);
          break;
        case 'ArrowUp': // select previous element
          event.preventDefault();
          this.focusElem(item.previousElementSibling as HTMLElement, item);
          break;
        case 'Escape': // close menu
          event.preventDefault();
          item.tabIndex = -1;
          this.toggleMenu();
          break;
      }
      if (event.key === 'ArrowDown' || event.key === 'ArrowUp') {

        if (commitIdx) this.highlight(this.commits[Number(commitIdx)]);

import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
  registerShortcut({
    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: link,
    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));
```

     5	## What changed and why
     6
     7	On GitHub, `c` starts a new issue or pull request from the list, and opens the commit picker on a pull request's changed files. Gitea had no such shortcut. Building on #56's registry and #58's link shortcuts, this PR adds `c` in those three places.
     8
     9	- **The create buttons declare `c` themselves.** "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are links, so they declare `c` the same way #58's tabs declare their `g` shortcuts, and `c` goes where the button leads, exactly as a click would. When the repository uses issue templates, that is the template chooser.
    10	- **Only a button that really creates something declares it.** An archived repository has no create button, and its pull request list shows "Compare commits" in that place; a "New Pull Request" button the user can't use is greyed out. The list page already decides all of this, so in each of these cases `c` simply doesn't exist.
    11	- **The commit picker declares `c` itself.** It is a Vue component that builds its own button, so it adds `c` when it appears on the "Files changed" tab. `c` opens it the same way a click does: focus moves to the picker's button first, so Escape works even while the commits are still loading, then to its first entry. `c` never closes it.

     1	## Design Decisions - @ab-wm
     2
     3	### Decisions for Commit 1
     4	#### Decision 1: The create button's link in the list declares `c`, and only when it really creates something
     5
     6	**Decision:** On the issue and pull request lists, the "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" buttons declare `c` in the page's HTML, the same way the tabs declare their `g` shortcuts (#58), so `c` goes where the button leads. The page only declares it when the button is shown and can be used.

### Decisions for Commit 2
#### Decision 2: The commit picker declares `c` itself, and `c` only ever opens it

**Decision:** The commit picker on the "Files changed" tab adds its own `c` shortcut when it appears on the page. Pressing `c` opens the picker the same way a click does, and does nothing when it is already open.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A new general attribute in the page's HTML that makes a shortcut click an element, like the one #58 added for links. (b) The page code that sets up the picker adds `c` from outside and clicks the picker's button.
**Rationale:** The picker's button is built by the picker itself after the page loads, and a click opens or closes it. Only the picker knows whether it is open, and it already has its translated label ("Filter by commit"). Declaring `c` inside the picker lets `c` open it through the same steps a click takes, so the first entry gets focus and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click (AC4), without ever closing it by accident. (a) would add a general mechanism for a single use, would have to reach inside the picker for a button that doesn't exist until the picker is built, and a click would close an open picker. (b) has the same closing problem and depends on the picker's inner markup from outside it.
**Consequences:** `c` only exists while the picker is on the page, so it is missing on the compare page and on an issue's own page (AC5). The picker gets its section ("Pull Requests", an existing string) from the page, the same way the "Go to file" box got its section in #56. This is the first shortcut a component adds from its own code instead of from the page's HTML.

// PullRequestContext contains context information for making a new pull request
type PullRequestContext struct {
	ctx *Context

	baseRepo, headRepo *repo_model.Repository

	canCreateNewPull    *bool
	defaultTargetBranch *string
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) SameRepo() bool {
	return prc.baseRepo != nil && prc.headRepo != nil && prc.baseRepo.ID == prc.headRepo.ID
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) CanCreateNewPull() bool {
	if prc.canCreateNewPull != nil {
		return *prc.canCreateNewPull
	}
	ctx := prc.ctx
	// People who have push access or have forked repository can propose a new pull request.
	can := prc.baseRepo.CanContentChange() &&
		(ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWrite(unit_model.TypeCode) || (ctx.IsSigned && repo_model.HasForkedRepo(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID)))
	prc.canCreateNewPull = &can
	return can
}

func (prc *PullRequestContext) MakeDefaultCompareLink(headBranch string) string {
	return prc.baseRepo.Link() + "/compare/" +
		util.PathEscapeSegments(prc.DefaultTargetBranch()) + "..." +
		util.Iif(prc.SameRepo(), "", util.PathEscapeSegments(prc.headRepo.OwnerName)+":") +
		util.PathEscapeSegments(headBranch)
}

export function initGlobalEnterQuickSubmit() {
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (e.key !== 'Enter') return;
    if (e.defaultPrevented) return; // a widget has handled it, e.g. a dropdown picking an item
    const el = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // an input in a normal form could handle Enter key by default, so we only handle the input outside a form
    const isEnterInBareInput = el.matches('input') && !el.closest('form');
    if ((isCtrlEnterInTextarea || isEnterInBareInput) && handleGlobalEnterQuickSubmit(el)) {
      e.preventDefault();
    }
  });
}

    actual=$(sha256sum "$DIR/$src" | cut -c1-16)
    if [ "$actual" != "$stored" ]; then
      err "$g" "DRIFT: $src changed since this guide was written (hash $stored, now $actual) - regenerate it (rule 18)"
    fi

    # rule 21: a guide may only cite paths its source doc already cites.
    # The doc's citations are its backticked tokens plus its scope: paths; trailing
    # slashes are normalised, and citing a directory whose files the doc cites is allowed.
    src_paths=$({ grep -oE '`[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+`' "$DIR/$src" | tr -d '`'
                  sed -n '2,10{/^scope:/p;}' "$DIR/$src" | sed 's/^scope: *//' | tr ',' '\n'
                } | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//; s|/*$||' | sort -u)
    while read -r path; do
      [ -n "$path" ] || continue
      printf '%s\n' "$src_paths" | grep -qxF "$path" && continue

   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

      scenario: A keyboard user opens the diff options menu (templates/repo/diff/options_dropdown.tmpl:1, a Fomantic dropdown with no search box) and types `c` to reach "Collapse all files" (line 15). Fomantic highlights that item without calling preventDefault (dropdown.js:1666-1670). The registry then runs the picker's action: focus jumps to the "Filter by commit" button, the options menu closes when it loses focus, and the commit picker opens with its first entry focused. The user asked for one menu item and ends up in a different menu.
  [7] (a11y-browsers, low) web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.vue:64 — The comment "where a click leaves it", the e2e comment at tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts:225 and the PR claim that `c` opens the picker "the same way a click does: focus moves to the picker's button first" are false in Safari and in Firefox on macOS, where clicking a button does not focus it.
      scenario: In Safari, a mouse click on the picker button leaves focus on the body. While the commits load, Escape after a click does nothing, because onKeyDown returns unless focus is inside the picker (DiffCommitSelector.vue:85). Escape after `c` does close the menu. AC4 still holds once the commits load, since both paths focus the first entry at line 152. Only the loading-time behaviour differs, and `c` is the better of the two. A grader on a Mac who compares click and `c` will see this, and it repeats the "false claim" problem already raised once. On the evidence: the PR says the Playwright tests pass on Chromium and Firefox and the hand check used headless Chromium, but playwright.config.ts:40 defines a webkit project and tools/test-e2e.sh:75 installs WebKit for CI. The click comparison was therefore never checked in a browser where it differs. A fix is to reword to "where a click leaves it in Chromium", or simply "so Escape works while the commits load".
  [8] (a11y-browsers, low) issue-59-pr-description.md:64 — `c` is a page-wide single-character shortcut with no way to turn it off or remap it, which falls under WCAG 2.1.4. The PR, design decisions and tech-debt files never mention that this is deferred to #60, and Tech Debt says "Introduced: None".
      scenario: WCAG 2.1.4 allows a single-key shortcut only if it can be turned off or remapped, or works only while its element has focus. Neither applies here: the registry listens on the whole document (shortcut.ts:135), and the picker's `c` is not limited to its own focus. A speech-input user, or someone with a tremor, who sends a stray `c` while focus is not in a text field is taken off the issue list in one keystroke. The deferral appears only in issue #59's out-of-scope list. The PR text mentions #56, #57 and #58 but not #60, and neither .specstory/issue-59-design-decisions.md nor issue-59-tech-debt.md mentions it. A reviewer will probably comment "single-key c with no off switch fails 2.1.4; where is this tracked?", and "Introduced: None" then reads as an oversight. One sentence pointing to #60 is enough to answer it.
  [9] (a11y-browsers, low) web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.vue:63 — When the picker is open but focus has moved out of it, `c` does nothing (the registry still calls preventDefault), so it does not bring focus back to the first entry as AC4 describes.
      scenario: A user opens the picker with `c` (or a click) and presses Tab. The menu has no focusout handling, so it stays visibly open while focus moves to the next control. Arrow keys and Escape no longer reach it, because onKeyDown requires focus inside the picker (line 85). Pressing `c` to get back in hits `if (this.menuVisible) return;`, so nothing happens and the key is still consumed. The open picker can then be reached only with Shift+Tab. A click on the button in the same state at least closes it. Focusing the menu's current item instead of returning would keep "never closes" and also meet AC4's "focus on its first entry".

     1	Title: feat(shortcut): c shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the commit picker
     2
     3	Closes #59
     4
     5	## What changed and why
     6
     7	On GitHub, `c` starts a new issue or pull request from the list, and opens the commit picker on a pull request's changed files. Gitea had no such shortcut. Building on #56's registry and #58's link shortcuts, this PR adds `c` in those three places.
     8
     9	- **The create buttons declare `c` themselves.** "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are links, so they declare `c` the same way #58's tabs declare their `g` shortcuts, and `c` goes where the button leads, exactly as a click would. When the repository uses issue templates, that is the template chooser.
    10	- **Only a button that really creates something declares it.** An archived repository has no create button, and its pull request list shows "Compare commits" in that place; a "New Pull Request" button the user can't use is greyed out. The list page already decides all of this, so in each of these cases `c` simply doesn't exist.
    11	- **The commit picker declares `c` itself.** It is a Vue component that builds its own button, so it adds `c` when it appears on the "Files changed" tab. `c` opens it the same way a click does: focus moves to the picker's button first, so Escape works even while the commits are still loading, then to its first entry. `c` never closes it.
    12	- **Each `c` is listed with what it opens** ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab, using existing strings, so nothing new needs translating.
    13	- The docs in `.claude-students` describe how a component adds its own shortcut.
    14
    15	## How the changes relate to the ACs
    16
    17	- **AC1:** `c` on the issue list goes where "New Issue" leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser.
    18	- **AC2:** `c` on the pull request list goes where "New Pull Request" leads.
    19	- **AC3:** a greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, and an archived repository's lists, declare no `c`, so it does nothing.
    20	- **AC4:** on the "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the commit picker with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click.
    21	- **AC5:** `c` only exists on those three pages, so it does nothing elsewhere; when `c` is the second key of `g c`, only `g c` runs.
    22	- **AC6:** each `c` is described by what it opens, under "Issues" on the lists and "Pull Requests" on the "Files changed" tab.
    23
    24	## How it was tested
    25
    26	### Test strategy
    27
    28	Almost all of this PR is wiring: which button declares `c` is decided by the list page, and the commit picker only exists on a real pull request. So the tests are Playwright tests on real pages.
    29
    30	- **One unit test, for what a page can't show yet.** Which shortcuts the picker lists isn't visible anywhere until #57's dialog exists, so `web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.test.ts` mounts the picker and checks that it lists `c` as "Filter by commit" in "Pull Requests" (AC6). Everything else is covered by earlier unit tests: #58's for a link turning into a shortcut, and #56's for `c` inside `g c`. Opening the picker is left to Playwright, because a unit test would have to fake the loading of the commits and the focus handling, and would mostly test the fakes.
    31	- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** Each of the 4 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the situation where a mistake would show. A signed-in user who can write to the repository, because only then is "New Pull Request" usable. A signed-out visitor, for whom it is greyed out, and an archived repository, where "Compare commits" takes its place and shares its `issue-list-new` class. A real pull request's "Files changed" tab, the only place the picker exists and the only way to see where focus lands, once normally and once with its commits held back, since focus only matters while they load.
    32	- **What "nothing happens" means here.** For AC3 the tests check that the page declares no `c`, instead of pressing `c` and waiting to see that nothing happened. Showing that a key didn't start a navigation races with whatever is pressed next, and whether `c` exists is decided by the declaration alone.
    33
    34	**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real: declaring `c` on the greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, declaring it on "Compare commits" in an archived repository, removing it from "New Issue", letting `c` close an open picker, opening it without moving focus to its button first, and, for the unit test, dropping the picker's section, changing its description and not registering `c` at all. Each break failed the matching test, and #56's and #58's tests stayed green.
    35
    36	**Not covered automatically, and why.** The template chooser isn't driven separately: "New Issue" links to it itself, and `c` goes wherever that link points. `c` doing nothing on an issue's own page, the compare page and a pull request's conversation tab was checked by hand, since there is no picker or create button there to declare it.
    37
    38	**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: both lists signed in and out, an archived repository, and a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, where `c` and a mouse click gave the same focus steps through the arrow keys.
    39
    40	| AC | What the tests check |
    41	| --- | --- |
    42	| AC1 | On the issue list, `c` goes to the new issue page |
    43	| AC2 | On the pull request list, `c` goes where "New Pull Request" leads |
    44	| AC3 | Signed out, the greyed-out "New Pull Request" declares no `c`; in an archived repository neither list declares `c`, though "Compare commits" is shown |
    45	| AC4 | On a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, `c` opens the picker with focus on its first entry, the arrow keys move within it, `c` again leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to its button, also while its commits are still loading |
    46	| AC5 | On the issue list, `g c` goes to the front page instead of starting a new issue |
    47	| AC6 | "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" are in "Issues"; the mounted picker lists `c` as "Filter by commit" in "Pull Requests" |

    49	## CI / manual verification
    50
    51	- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.
    52	- `make test-frontend`: 362 tests pass, including the new one.
    53	- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.

    56
    57	## Design
    58
    59	Design decisions noted under issue #59.
    60

    64	- None.

It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.
    68
    69	## Implementation Note
    70	Despite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. These shortcuts only take the user to another page or open the existing commit picker, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.

I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. AI-Log reference under related Issue #59.

     1	## Design Decisions - @ab-wm
     2
     3	### Decisions for Commit 1
     4	#### Decision 1: The create button's link in the list declares `c`, and only when it really creates something
     5
     6	**Decision:** On the issue and pull request lists, the "New Issue" and "New Pull Request" buttons declare `c` in the page's HTML, the same way the tabs declare their `g` shortcuts (#58).
     7	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The page code finds the create button and clicks it. (b) The server hands the page the address of the create page.
     8	**Rationale:** The list page already decides which button to show in the context of this page (archived repository, permissions, etc.). Declaring the shortcut on the button follows those decisions, so AC3 and AC5 need no rules of their own. (a) would have to tell the create button apart from "Compare commits", which shares its `issue-list-new` class, and check for the greyed-out state, repeating what the page already knows. (b) would repeat the same rules in a second place, where they could drift apart. Nothing else happens when the buttons are clicked, so going where the button leads is the same as clicking it (AC1, AC2).
     9	**Consequences:** No new page code: the buttons reuse #58's way of declaring a shortcut on a link, so #59 builds on #58. A greyed-out "New Pull Request" button still has an address, so the page must leave it undeclared, or `c` would go where a click can't.
    10
    11	### Decisions for Commit 2
    12	#### Decision 2: The commit picker declares `c` itself, and `c` only ever opens it
    13
    14	**Decision:** The commit picker on the "Files changed" tab adds its own `c` shortcut when it appears on the page. Pressing `c` opens the picker the same way a click does, and does nothing when it is already open.
    15	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A new general attribute in the page's HTML that makes a shortcut click an element, like the one #58 added for links. (b) The page code that sets up the picker adds `c` from outside and clicks the picker's button.
    16	**Rationale:** The picker's button is built by the picker itself after the page loads, and a click opens or closes it. Only the picker knows whether it is open, and it already has its translated label ("Filter by commit"). Declaring `c` inside the picker lets `c` open it through the same steps a click takes, so the first entry gets focus and the arrow keys and Escape work as after a click (AC4), without ever closing it by accident. (a) would add a general mechanism for a single use, would have to reach inside the picker for a button that doesn't exist until the picker is built, and a click would close an open picker. (b) has the same closing problem and depends on the picker's inner markup from outside it.
    17	**Consequences:** `c` only exists while the picker is on the page, so it is missing on the compare page and on an issue's own page (AC5). The picker gets its section ("Pull Requests", an existing string) from the page, the same way the "Go to file" box got its section in #56. This is the first shortcut a component adds from its own code instead of from the page's HTML.
----

It does the same after a click, so `c` matches a click as AC4 asks; changing the picker is out of #59's scope. Not fixed here.

+// a pull request with one commit; returns its "Files changed" tab
+async function createPullRequest(page: Page) {

+  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
+  await apiCreateFile(page.request, owner, repoName, 'feature.txt', 'feature', {newBranch: 'feature'});
+  const index = await apiCreatePR(page.request, owner, repoName, 'feature', 'main', 'picker');
+  return `${repoLink}/pulls/${index}/files`;
+}

+  await page.keyboard.press('c');

+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
+  await expect(showAll).not.toBeFocused();
+  await expect(menu.locator(':focus')).toHaveCount(1); // the arrow keys move within the menu
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');

<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read PR rubric and AI section rules

`cd /home/mantmant/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/.claude-students && sed -n 160,215p COURSE-WORKFLOW.md; echo ----; sed -n 25,75p AI-ASSISTANCE.md`

```text
## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## UML diagrams (D6)

The person who resolved a medium issue draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram for it. Several
small issues that together equal one medium issue are drawn together instead. Files:
----
- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
```

function attachDomEvents(dropdown: HTMLElement, focusable: HTMLElement, menu: HTMLElement) {

    // otherwise use the "selected" for combobox (for the last selected item)
    const active = $(menu).find('> .item.active, > .item.selected, > .scrolling.menu > .item.selected')[0];

      focusable.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant');

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 02:59:39Z)**_

Here's the second pass, with 1 finding refuted.

**Real bug (confirmed, and reproduced just now)**

**5 + 6. Type-ahead in Fomantic dropdowns triggers `c`.**
- On the issue list, focus in the "Type" filter and press `c` to jump to "Created by you", and you land on `/issues/new` instead. On the PR list you land on the compare page. On "Files changed", `c` in the options menu (for "Collapse all files") opens the commit picker.
- **Cause:** a Fomantic dropdown without a search box jumps to the first item starting with the typed letter (`web_src/fomantic/build/components/dropdown.js:1666-1670`), but never marks the key as used. So #56's rule "a key a widget already used runs no shortcut" can't see it.
- It isn't new to #59: typing `g` then `i` in such a dropdown would fire #58's `g i` the same way. `c` just makes it likely, because it's the first letter of real menu items.

**Small, quick fixes**

| # | Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | The loading test doesn't assert that focus returns to the button, though the PR's AC4 row claims it. It also ends without waiting for the released response. | Add the focus check, then wait for the response before the final checks. |
| 1 | AC1's template chooser case is never driven, and one template file would cover it. | Add it to test 1. |
| 4 | PR: "only then is New Pull Request usable" is wrong, because a fork also enables it. | Reword. |
| 3 | Decision 1: "AC3 needs no rules of its own" vs the `CanCreateNewPull` condition in the template. | Reword. |
| 7 | "Where a click leaves it" isn't true in Safari or Firefox on macOS, where a click doesn't focus a button. | Reword the code comment, the test comment and the PR line. |
| 0 | Every check the PR reports was Claude's. A grader may want your own. | Add a line saying what you tried yourself, as you did on #58. |

**Skipped:**
- WCAG 2.1.4 and `#60` (refuted, since `s` already existed before #59). A one-line mention of #60 is cheap if you want it.
- `c` doing nothing when the picker is open but focus has left it. That's Decision 2 working as designed, and the picker's behaviour is out of scope.

**#59, Decision 3: how to stop type-ahead in a dropdown from running shortcuts**

- **(a) Fix the dropdown.** Gitea's own dropdown patch (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts:275`) would mark a single letter as used when the dropdown has no search box, because that dropdown uses letters to jump to an item. #56's existing rule then skips it.
  - This is the same contract `<aria-menu>` already follows for #56's AC7.
  - The registry doesn't change, and every shortcut benefits: `s`, `t`, the `g` keys and `c`.
- **(b) Teach the registry about dropdowns:** ignore keys while focus is inside `.ui.dropdown` or any menu or listbox. Simpler to write, but the general registry would then depend on Fomantic's class names, and it changes #56's rules for every page.
- **(c) Leave it** and list it under Tech Debt.

I recommend **(a)**. It fixes the widget that misbehaves, at the place #56 already expects widgets to report keys they used.

import '../../../fomantic/build/fomantic.js';
import {createElementFromHTML} from '../../utils/dom.ts';
import {hideScopedEmptyDividers, initAriaDropdownPatch} from './dropdown.ts';
import {initFomanticTransition} from './transition.ts';

$.fn.fomanticExt = {};
initFomanticTransition(); // labels of multiple selection dropdowns are shown with a transition
initAriaDropdownPatch();

// values are IDs, as in the protected branch user pickers, so a name taken from the value is wrong
function createMultipleDropdown(value: string) {
  const el = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`<div class="ui multiple selection dropdown">
  <input type="hidden" value="${value}">
  <div class="text"></div>
  <div class="menu">
    <div class="item" data-value="1">Alpha</div>
    <div class="item" data-value="2">Beta</div>
  </div>
</div>`);
  document.body.append(el);
  $(el).dropdown();
  return el;
}

describe('multiple selection aria', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    window.config.i18n.remove_label_str = 'Remove item "%s"';
    window.config.i18n.selected_item_str = 'Selected "%s"';
    window.config.i18n.deselected_item_str = 'Deselected "%s"';
  });
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
    document.body.replaceChildren();
  });

  test('AC4: delete icons are named by the label text, not the value', () => {
    window.config.runModeIsProd = false;
    const el = initDropdown(html);
    expect(warningsAbout(el)).toBe(0);
  });
});

Append Decision 3 to both decision files

```bash
cd /home/mantmant/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/.specstory && python3 - <<'EOF'
block = '''
### Decisions for Commit 8
#### Decision 3: A dropdown that jumps to an item on a typed letter marks that key as used

**Decision:** When one of Gitea's older dropdowns without a search box uses a typed letter to jump to an item, it now marks the key as used, so no keyboard shortcut runs on it. This covers every such dropdown, not just the filters on the lists.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Make the shortcut code itself ignore every key while focus is inside any dropdown or menu. (b) Leave it, and list it under Tech Debt.
**Rationale:** The shortcut code already skips a key that a widget on the page has used (#56), and the newer menus say when they use one. These older dropdowns jump to an item but never say so, so typing "c" in the issue list's "Type" filter left for the new issue page instead of picking "Created by you". Fixing the dropdown puts the fix where the problem is, and every shortcut benefits: `s`, `t`, the `g` keys and `c`. (a) would also work, but the general shortcut code would have to know one widget library's class names, and it would change #56's rules on every page. (b) would leave a shortcut that throws users off the page while they are picking a filter.
**Consequences:** Keys pressed with Ctrl, Alt or Cmd and the space bar are left alone, and a dropdown with a search box is untouched, so typing into it still works. The change lives in Gitea's patch for the older dropdowns, which are on their way out, so it goes away with them.
'''
for p in ['issue-59-design-decisions.md', 'decisions.md']:
    s = open(p).read().rstrip('\n') + '\n' + block
    open(p, 'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -c "Decision 3" decisions.md issue-59-design-decisions.md
```

### Test strategy

Almost all of this PR is wiring: which button declares `c` is decided by the list page, and the commit picker only exists on a real pull request. So the tests are Playwright tests on real pages.

- **Unit tests for what a page can't show.** Which shortcuts the picker lists isn't visible anywhere until #57's dialog exists, so `web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.test.ts` mounts the picker and checks that it lists `c` as "Filter by commit" in "Pull Requests" (AC6). Whether a dropdown marks a typed letter as used is invisible on a page too, so two tests in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.test.ts` check it directly: a letter in a dropdown without a search box is used, Ctrl+C isn't, and typing into a search box is left alone. Everything else is covered by earlier unit tests: #58's for a link turning into a shortcut, and #56's for `c` inside `g c`. Opening the picker is left to Playwright, because a unit test would have to fake the loading of the commits and the focus handling, and would mostly test the fakes.
- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** Each of the 5 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the situation where a mistake would show. A signed-in user who can write to the repository, because "New Pull Request" is only usable with write access or a fork; the same repository with an issue template, where "New Issue" leads to the chooser instead. Focus in the "Type" filter, the one place on the list where `c` is also a menu's own letter. A signed-out visitor, for whom it is greyed out, and an archived repository, where "Compare commits" takes its place and shares its `issue-list-new` class. A real pull request's "Files changed" tab, the only place the picker exists and the only way to see where focus lands, once normally and once with its commits held back, since focus only matters while they load.
- **What "nothing happens" means here.** For AC3 the tests check that the page declares no `c`, instead of pressing `c` and waiting to see that nothing happened. Showing that a key didn't start a navigation races with whatever is pressed next, and whether `c` exists is decided by the declaration alone.

**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real: declaring `c` on the greyed-out "New Pull Request" button, declaring it on "Compare commits" in an archived repository, removing it from "New Issue", letting `c` close an open picker, opening it without moving focus to its button first, and removing the dropdown fix. For the unit tests: dropping the picker's section, changing its description, not registering `c` at all, and for the dropdown, not marking the letter, marking it inside a search box too, and marking it with Ctrl. Each break failed the matching test, and #56's and #58's tests stayed green.

**Not covered automatically, and why.** `c` doing nothing on an issue's own page, the compare page and a pull request's conversation tab was checked by hand, since there is no picker or create button there to declare it.

**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: both lists signed in and out, an archived repository, and a real pull request's "Files changed" tab, where `c` and a mouse click gave the same focus steps through the arrow keys. I personally spot checked the features to ensure the features work as expected, such as on the issue list, in the filter, and on a pull request's "Files changed" tab.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | On the issue list, `c` goes to the new issue page, and to the template chooser once the repository has an issue template |
| AC2 | On the pull request list, `c` goes where "New Pull Request" leads |
```
