127:{"assignees":[{"id":"U_kgDOC65pPg","login":"ab-wm","name":"","databaseId":195979582}],"body":"> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1 (foundation)** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by nothing\n\n## User Story\nAs a Gitea user who navigates by keyboard, I want shortcuts to be declared in one place with\nsupport for key sequences and modifiers, so that new shortcuts can be added consistently and\nlisted in one dialog instead of being hard-coded one at a time.\n\n## User Scenario\nNothing visible changes for an end user in this issue: pressing `s` on a repository home page\nstill focuses the sidebar search, and `t` on the code view still opens the file finder. What\nchanges is underneath — a developer adding a shortcut now calls `registerShortcut()` with the\nkeys, a category and a description, instead of adding another branch to the global `keydown`\nhandler. The next two issues (the help dialog and the `g` chords) read that registry.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] AC1: Given the repo home page, when the user presses `s` outside an input, then the sidebar\n      search input receives focus and the `<kbd>S</kbd>` hint hides — i.e. the behaviour in\n      `templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl` is unchanged after the refactor.\n- [ ] AC2: Given a shortcut registered as a two-key sequence `g c`, when the user presses `g` then\n      `c` within the chord timeout, then its handler runs exactly once and neither key reaches its\n      own single-key handler.\n- [ ] AC3: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than the chord\n      timeout before pressing `c`, then the sequence is abandoned and `c`'s own single-key\n      shortcut runs instead.\n- [ ] AC4: Given focus is inside an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or a `contenteditable` element,\n      when any registered character shortcut key is pressed, then no shortcut handler runs and the\n      keystroke is not prevented.\n- [ ] AC5: Given a shortcut registered with a modifier (for example `mod+k`), when the user\n      presses it, then the handler runs — the current unconditional bail-out on\n      `ctrlKey || metaKey || altKey` (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts:35`) no longer blocks it.\n- [ ] AC6: Given two calls to `registerShortcut` with the same key sequence, when the second one\n      runs, then it throws, so a duplicate binding fails at startup rather than silently shadowing.\n- [ ] AC7: `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` exists and covers AC2–AC6 with `pnpm exec vitest\n      shortcut`, with no browser needed.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Any new user-facing shortcut. `s` and `t` stay the only two bindings after this issue.\n- The help dialog (#57) and the ability to turn shortcuts off (#60).\n- Remapping shortcuts, or persisting anything to the server.\n- The editor-local key handling in `web_src/js/modules/codeeditor/` and\n  `web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`; those stay where they are.\n\n## Open Questions\n- Chord timeout length. 1500 ms is proposed; GitHub's is roughly a second. Settle it in review.\n- Whether `mod` should normalise to Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Proposed: yes, one `mod`\n  token, since no shortcut should ever need to distinguish them.\n\n## Design Decision\n**Decision:** Keep one document-level `keydown` listener, but move the binding table out of the\nDOM and into a JS registry module, and keep the existing `<kbd data-shortcut-keys>` markup working\nby having `initShortcutKbd` register a focus handler for each `<kbd>` it initialises.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the DOM as the source of truth and extend the\n`querySelector('.global-shortcut-wrapper > kbd[data-shortcut-keys=...]')` lookup on line 57 with\nsequence and modifier parsing. (b) Attach per-element listeners via `registerGlobalInitFunc`, one\nper shortcut-bearing element, and drop the global listener.\n\n**Rationale:** (a) cannot express a shortcut that has no input to focus — a `g c` navigation chord\nor a help dialog has no `<kbd>` sibling to find, and the help dialog in #57 needs to enumerate\nevery shortcut, which a DOM query over hidden and not-yet-rendered elements cannot do. (b) breaks\nchords outright, because the first key of a sequence is pressed while focus is on the document,\nnot on any particular element. A registry keeps one listener, gives #57 something to enumerate,\nand is unit-testable without a DOM fixture per case.\n\n**Consequences:** Easier — adding a shortcut becomes one call, and shortcuts with no associated\nelement become possible for the first time. Harder — the registry is module state that must be\npopulated before the first keypress, so registration has to happen during page init, and a\nregistry that is not reset between tests will leak bindings across test cases; the module needs an\nexported reset used only by tests. It also adds a second place to look when debugging a key, since\nthe `<kbd>` markup no longer tells the whole story.\n\n## Scope\nmedium (5 points)\n\n---\n\n---\n*Spec drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5) from `docs/sprint1/backlog-refinement.md`, posted by @Jack-Donohue.*","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAACtk8WWQ","name":"enhancement","description":"New feature or request","color":"a2eeef"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC0JZx6A","name":"scope: medium","description":"","color":"1545a8"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC5MNkTw","name":"Deferred","description":"","color":"aaaaaa"}],"milestone":null,"number":56,"state":"OPEN","title":"Central keyboard-shortcut registry with chords and modifiers"}
129:{"assignees":[{"id":"U_kgDOC65pPg","login":"ab-wm","name":"","databaseId":195979582}],"body":"> Sub-issue of #23 · **P2 — only if capacity allows** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56\n\n## User Story\nAs a user working inside a repository, I want to jump between its code, issues, pull requests and\nactions with two-key `g` sequences, so that I can move around without taking my hands off the\nkeyboard or hunting for the tab.\n\n## User Scenario\nA reviewer is reading a file in a repository. They press `g` then `i` and land on that\nrepository's issue list. They press `g` then `p` and land on the pull request list. On a\nrepository with the wiki disabled, pressing `g` then `w` does nothing at all — no navigation, no\nerror.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] AC1: Given any page inside a repository, when the user presses `g` then `c`, then the\n      browser navigates to that repository's code tab.\n- [ ] AC2: Given the same, `g i` goes to Issues, `g p` to Pull requests, `g a` to Actions and\n      `g r` to Releases.\n- [ ] AC3: Given a repository whose issue unit is disabled, when the user presses `g` then `i`,\n      then nothing happens and the page does not navigate.\n- [ ] AC4: Given a page outside any repository, when the user presses `g` then `i`, then nothing\n      happens.\n- [ ] AC5: Given focus is in the issue comment textarea, when the user types `g` then `i`, then\n      the literal text \"gi\" is inserted and the page does not navigate.\n- [ ] AC6: Given #57 is merged, when the help dialog is opened inside a repository, then every\n      `g` shortcut that is currently active appears there, and ones disabled by AC3 do not.\n- [ ] AC7: A Playwright test covers AC1, AC3 and AC5 against a fixture repository.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Global (non-repository) chords such as `g d` for the dashboard or `g n` for notifications.\n  They can follow in Sprint 2 once the pattern is proven.\n- Shortcuts that act on the current page rather than navigating (assigning labels, closing an\n  issue).\n- Changing the repository navigation markup itself.\n\n## Open Questions\n- `g r` for Releases collides with nothing today, but GitHub does not use it; confirm the letter\n  set with the team during spec review.\n\n## Design Decision\n**Decision:** Resolve each `g` target by reading the href off the already-rendered repository\nnavigation links in the DOM, rather than by constructing URLs from repository data passed through\n`pageData`.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Emit the repository owner and name into `pageData` and build\n`/{owner}/{repo}/issues` in JS. (b) Add a new field to `pageData` listing the enabled units and\ntheir URLs, populated server-side in the repo context.\n\n**Rationale:** The navigation bar already renders exactly the tabs the current user may see — the\nserver has resolved units, permissions and the `AppSubUrl` prefix. Reading the href reuses that\nwork, so AC3 and AC4 fall out for free: no link, no shortcut. (a) would have to duplicate the unit\nand permission checks in JS and would get `AppSubUrl` sub-path installs wrong. (b) is correct but\nadds a server-side payload to every page for a client-side convenience.\n\n**Consequences:** Easier — permissions, disabled units and sub-path installs are handled without\nany new server code, and a repo the user cannot see issues on simply has no `g i`. Harder — the\nshortcuts are now coupled to the repository nav's markup, so a future refactor of that template\ncan silently break them; the e2e test in AC7 is what catches that, and the selector used needs a\ncomment saying why.\n\n## Scope\nmedium (5 points)\n\n---\n\n---\n*Spec drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5) from `docs/sprint1/backlog-refinement.md`, posted by @Jack-Donohue.*","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAACtk8WWQ","name":"enhancement","description":"New feature or request","color":"a2eeef"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC0JZx6A","name":"scope: medium","description":"","color":"1545a8"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC5MNkTw","name":"Deferred","description":"","color":"aaaaaa"}],"milestone":{"number":3,"title":"Sprint 2","description":"","dueOn":null},"number":58,"state":"OPEN","title":"`g`-chord navigation shortcuts across repo and global pages"}

################ ISSUE 58
`g` navigation shortcuts for repository tabs and notifications ['enhancement', 'scope: medium']
## User Story

As a Gitea user who knows GitHub's keyboard shortcuts, I want the same two-key `g` shortcuts to perform the same behavior, taking me to a repository's code, issues, pull requests, actions and wiki, an

## User Scenario
A reviewer is reading a file on a feature branch. They press `g` then `i` and land on the repository's issue list, then `g` then `p` for the pull request list. Pressing `g` then `c` takes them back to

A shortcut only works when its tab is shown. On a repository with the wiki turned off, or one that uses an external wiki, pressing `g` then `w` does nothing at all: no navigation, no error.

| Keys | Goes to | Works when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `g c` | The repository's front page, default branch | The Code tab is shown |

// make the item has role=option/menuitem, add an id if there wasn't one yet, make items as non-focusable
// the elements inside the dropdown menu item should not be focusable, the focus should always be on the dropdown primary element.
function updateMenuItem(dropdown: HTMLElement, item: HTMLElement) {
  if (!item.id) item.id = generateElemId('_aria_dropdown_item_');
  item.setAttribute('role', (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listItemRole);
  item.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
  for (const el of item.querySelectorAll('a, input, button')) el.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
}
/**
 * make the label item and its "delete icon" have correct aria attributes
 * @param {HTMLElement} label
 */
function updateSelectionLabel(label: HTMLElement) {
  // the "label" is like this: "<a|div class="ui label" data-value="1">the-label-name <i|svg class="delete icon"/></a>"
  if (!label.id) {
    label.id = generateElemId('_aria_dropdown_label_');
    if (e.key === 'Enter') {
      const elItem = menu.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .item.selected, .menu > .item.selected');
      // if the selected item is clickable, then trigger the click event.
      // we can not click any item without check, because Fomantic code might also handle the Enter event. that would result in double click.
      if (elItem?.matches('a, .js-aria-clickable') && !elItem.matches('.tw-hidden, .filtered')) {
        e.preventDefault();
        elItem.click();
      }
    }
    // without a search box, Fomantic jumps to the item starting with a typed letter, so the key is used here and runs no page shortcut
    if (focusable === dropdown && e.key.length === 1 && e.key !== ' ' && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) e.preventDefault();
  });

CodeRabbit's comment is fixed, and staged for you to commit. It was a real bug, worse than its comment said.

**The bug.** Before agreeing, I tested it on a real page with an A/B comparison:
- With my earlier dropdown fix, typing into a filter box that sits *inside* a dropdown's menu was blocked. That includes the list page's Label filter and the issue sidebar's label picker; milestones and assignees use the same layout.
- Without the fix, both boxes took "cob". With it, both stayed empty.
- The cause: my check only recognised the `input.search` layout, and it also caught keys typed into inputs inside the dropdown. None of my tests typed into such a box, which is why it slipped through.

**What's staged**
- **`dropdown.ts`:** a letter is marked as used only when it's typed **on the dropdown itself** (`e.target === dropdown`), and only when **Fomantic itself** says there's no search box (`$(dropdown).dropdown('has search')`, the same call style as `dropdown.ts:84`). So a letter typed into any input inside, and every in-menu filter box, are left alone.
- **`dropdown.test.ts`:** two additions.
  - An input inside a menu item still takes typing. That's CodeRabbit's case.
  - A dropdown whose search box sits in its menu leaves letters alone, both in the box and on the dropdown.
- **New Playwright test, "a list filter with its own search box still takes typing":** it creates a label, opens the Label filter and types "cob" into it.

**Checked**
- On the real page, both filter boxes take typing, and `c` in the "Type" filter still picks its item.
- **Unit tests:** each of three breaks fails them: the old condition, the target check alone, and the Fomantic check alone.
- The new Playwright test fails on the old condition (expected "cob", received "").
- `make test-frontend` passes 365 tests. `shortcut` and `menus` pass 38/38 on both browsers. `make lint-js` passes.
